data.author: Siah
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）代理从经验中学习的进展及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [kubb] 对AI代理从经验中学习的技术进步感到兴奋，并设想利用这种技术创建自动化的商业和娱乐工具，例如自动赚钱的SaaS公司和根据个人喜好生成游戏的代理。
• [jgbmlg] 认为在人类智力下降的时代，机器智力的进步具有讽刺意味。
• [0xCE0] 对科学论文缺乏出版日期表示不满，这影响了对论文时效性的判断。
• [artninja1988] 引用了DeepMind的论文，但对“奖励就足够”的假设持怀疑态度，认为固定奖励功能的AI并不等同于通用人工智能（AGI）。
• [quantumHazer] 怀疑此类文章是公关噱头，对文章的实质内容和图表表示不满，并表达了对过度炒作的疲惫感。
• [simianwords] 关注“从经验中学习”是否仍然通过离线的强化学习（RL）实现，而不是自主和持续地学习，并对论文中提到的学习方式产生误解。
• [ChrisArchitect] 引用Richard Sutton的观点，将相关讨论置于更广泛的AI设计框架中。
• [tempodox] 怀疑文章本身是由语言模型（LLM）生成的。
• [numpad0] 认为机器能够实时学习和适应才是AI的真正目标，而不是仅依靠大规模数据集进行训练。
• [kkfx] 认为知识应用的自动化将增加，但知识创造仍需人类参与，并提出谁拥有模型的问题，担心当前由大公司主导的模式可能带来的社会影响。
• [baq] 提醒读者在阅读相关文章或书籍时，应考虑人工智能快速发展的潜在影响，特别是在本世纪20年代末可能发生的技术突破。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括AI代理从经验中学习的实际应用范围、奖励机制是否足以实现通用人工智能，以及当前AI技术发展过程中大公司主导模式的潜在风险。
• 讨论还涉及对科学论文缺乏出版日期的实际影响、文章内容的真实性及其是否为公关噱头的质疑。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是知识创造与应用的未来分工，以及模型所有权和开放知识的问题。

data.title: Healthy soil is the hidden ingredient
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了欧洲土壤健康问题，尤其是西班牙的土壤退化状况。欧盟60-70%的土壤处于不健康状态，导致每年约€500亿的损失。西班牙是土壤侵蚀最严重的国家，每年每公顷流失约14.2吨土壤。地理学家Jesús Rodrigo Comino通过地理绘图系统和人工智能研究葡萄园的土壤侵蚀，致力于开发可持续的土壤管理实践，帮助农民做出决策，如灌溉和种植覆盖作物。他还参与了欧盟的SOILCRATES项目，旨在通过实验提高人们对土壤健康的认识。气候变化对土壤健康的影响日益显著，如气温升高和极端降雨事件增加。尽管有些农民开始采用良好实践，但仍需更多努力改善土壤质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：土壤健康与改良方法及其相关技术应用

不同观点：
• [econ] 和 [pdfernhout] 提到古代文明可能已经深入研究过土壤改良（如Terra Preta），并提出现代方法如岩石粉末（rock dust）可以有效恢复土壤肥力。他们强调了长期研究和历史经验在土壤管理中的价值。
• [bgnn] 分享了个人园艺经验，强调了通过堆肥、无挖耕作等方式改良土壤的过程，并指出与微生物互动和自然实验的重要性。尽管过程复杂且存在失败，但通过持续努力可以获得成功。
• [contingencies] 也分享了在贫瘠土壤上种植的经验，通过改变植物种类、覆盖物和有机废物等方式逐步改善土壤质量。重点在于耐心地通过多种方法结合来改善不同类型的土壤。
• [ralusek] 对土壤健康的神秘化提出质疑，认为植物基本需求只是水、光和肥料，并指出通过合成肥料和土壤添加剂也可以实现植物健康生长。不过，他也承认培养良好的土壤可以实现自我维持，减少额外输入。

补充讨论：
• [tbrownaw] 和 [zeristor] 提到了使用人工智能（AI）和地理信息系统（GIS）等技术来评估和改善土壤质量，表明科技在土壤管理中的潜在应用。
• [jimbobthemighty] 分享了一篇关于植物“垃圾食品”问题的文章，强调不良土壤管理可能导致的问题。
• [photochemsyn] 提出了重金属污染对土壤健康的威胁，强调了工业和矿业历史对农业土壤的潜在风险，并引用了相关文献支持其观点。
• [bethekidyouwant] 质疑了关于健康土壤的浪漫化描述，指出大规模农业生产中依赖人工劳动改良土壤的不现实性。
• [poorna12] 提到了Sadhguru通过骑行活动传播保护土壤的信息，强调了公众意识在土壤保护中的重要性。
• [SwayamDas] 总结了改良土壤所需的主要成分，包括有机物、微生物、土壤动物、养分、土壤结构和水管理，提供了一个综合的土壤改良框架。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否需要依赖合成肥料和土壤添加剂来实现植物健康生长存在争议。
• 有人质疑土壤健康管理中的神秘化和浪漫化描述，认为科技和合成方法也能有效改良土壤。
• 重金属污染问题在土壤健康讨论中被提出，但其实际监测和标准执行存在争议。

总结：评论主要围绕土壤改良方法、个人经验分享、科技应用及相关争议展开，涉及历史经验、现代科技、合成与自然方法的比较以及重金属污染等多个方面。

Soil quality is crucial for sustaining production in vineyards, such as this one near Montilla in southern Spain.
Credit: JORGE GUERRERO/AFP via Getty
When it comes to the land, the European Union faces a reckoning: 60–70% of its soils are considered unhealthy, resulting in soil degradation. That costs €50 billion (US$55 billion) annually because of the loss of essential services and the effect on human health. Spain has the highest rates of soil degradation in Europe, with an average of 14.2 tonnes of soil lost per hectare to erosion each year
1
. Although its importance is often overlooked, quality soil is essential for sustaining agriculture and crucial ecosystems. Its importance was highlighted in the 2015 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, with soil health named as a key factor in achieving several of the goals.
Nature Spotlight: Spain
Having studied soil erosion in vineyards across Europe, Jesús Rodrigo Comino, a geographer at the University of Granada, Spain, is hoping to unearth a solution. Now he works with farmers, researchers and policymakers to test and use more-sustainable soil-management practices in vineyards and more broadly. Rodrigo Comino speaks to
Nature
about his research programme and why healthy soils are important for Spain’s cultural heritage and economy.
Tell us about your work in soil science.
I was always a curious kid, but my passion for soil science began with my studies at the University of Malaga in Spain and at Trier University in Germany. My home region of Andalusia in Spain has some really beautiful landscapes, but some areas are heavily degraded because of soil erosion and other factors. I felt compelled to find solutions to these problems.
When I came back to Spain in 2021 after doing my PhD and a postdoctoral position in Germany, I started a project to assess soil erosion and degradation in vineyards using geographical mapping systems and artificial intelligence (AI). Soil erosion is caused by natural factors, such as extreme rainfall events and strong winds, as well as by human-driven activities, including tillage and urbanization. AI helps me to design and polish the software codes that I use to create geographical maps and analyse data. The main idea is to develop tools to help farmers make decisions. These might be about how to apply irrigation systems; which types of cover crop to plant; or when to till the soil, if necessary, to prevent soil degradation.
Geographer Jesús Rodrigo Comino examines the soil at a vineyard.
Credit: Jesús Rodrigo Comino
I’m also involved in a Soil Living Labs project called SOILCRATES, which is part of an EU mission called A Soil Deal for Europe. The goal is to create field sites where soil scientists, agronomists, stakeholders and policymakers come together to conduct experiments and establish plots with sustainable soils. As part of the project, we also aim to show people how important fertile soils are to their lives and how their actions can affect soil health. The EU is now investing in a variety of projects to improve soil quality and enhance people’s understanding of soil. I’ve seen people implementing good practices to reduce soil erosion. But we’re not there yet — much more work is needed.
How has climate change affected your work?
It is evident that many places, especially urban ones, are experiencing an increase in temperature and a reduction in precipitation volume. We’re also seeing a concentration of extreme rainfall events in short periods of time, such as the flooding that happened in Valencia in Spain last year. All of these factors can affect soil health.
When it comes to the vineyards in Spain, we don’t yet have enough data to confirm whether and how climate change is altering them — but the trends are clear. We know that vineyards are encountering higher temperatures now than they did in the past, and that this is causing the vines to flower earlier. Annual rainfall is being concentrated into shorter time periods, and we’re also experiencing extreme rainfall events, which cause soil erosion.
What are farmers telling you about their experiences?

data.title: Signal Carnival
data.author: adunk
data.article_summary: 《Signal Carnival》是Revision 2025上发布的一款C64演示，要求用户切换音频和视频线以体验独特效果。该创意源于90年代将音频连接到视频的操作，但《Signal Carnival》首次实现了音视频线同时互换，且保持音画正常输出。技术上，利用C64的VIC芯片以高频生成音频，通过调整亮度控制音量和波形。视频则通过SID芯片的音量寄存器生成，但由于内部带通滤波器，像素模糊，水平分辨率受限。演示加载过程中持续进行音频输出，并采用自定义加载器处理数据解码和效果生成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对音视频技术结合演示的评论和讨论

不同观点：
• Flow认为演示非常酷，并提出一个技术性问题：是用音频芯片制作视频更难，还是用视频芯片制作音频更难。这引发了对技术挑战的思考。
• olelele最初以为帖子内容与 messaging service 和美国政治有关，但发现是音视频演示后表示欣赏和喜爱。
• franky47对同时通过视频和音频发送相同信号的效果感到好奇，认为尽管可能不如演示效果好，但某些信号组合可能会产生有趣的结果。
• wasabi991011提醒其他可能困惑的用户点击页面上的YouTube链接观看视频，并称赞演示效果非常酷。
• jwr表达了对这种技术性内容的喜爱，特别提到了“hack value”（黑客价值），显示出对创新和创意内容的兴趣。
• WorldPeas提问是否有人尝试过在现代计算机上进行类似操作，并询问是否能从音视频中获得更多“horsepower”（性能或效果）。
• barbazoo简单表达了对演示的欣赏，称之为美丽的事情。
• layer8表示希望看到和听到正确插接版本的视频，可能暗示对技术实现的细节有更高要求。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术性问题和对创新内容的兴趣显示出社区对技术实验和创意演示的关注。
• 不同用户对演示效果的欣赏以及对技术细节的探讨构成了评论的主要内容。
• 争议焦点并不明显，但部分用户对技术实现细节和效果优化表现出更高期待。

43745040.article_content:
At Revision 2025, we released "Signal Carnival" (
csdb
,
YouTube
). This demo asks you to
switch the audio and video cable of your C64:
(
Diagram by Felidae
)
Technically, "misplugging" those cables is not a completely new idea. In the
90s, it was a common thing to connect audio to both speaker and video,
to get screen flickering timed with the music beats.
However, "Signal Carnival" is the first production to switch both these
cables, while still being able to play meaningful audio and video.
How to drive audio using a video signal
The C64's VIC chip operates at a frequency of 7.9Mhz, and new values can be
written to it by the 6502 at a rate of up to 246kHz. Since even high
quality audio rarely exceeds 44kHz, this is easily a high enough frequency
to generate music.
Inspired by the music routine from freespin, we combined two timers to
get an interesting waveform, which is adjusted once per frame. This is
the code that drives audio:
lda $dc06
ora $dd06
eor $02
sta $d020
Here,
$dc06
and
$dd06
are the lower bytes of the B timers of CIA #1 and #2,
respectively. They're in turn increased every time their A timers
overflow. And those are set to a new value for every new note.
Eor-ing with the value at zeropage
$02
allows to slightly tweak the waveform (and volume!),
and then the result is written to
$d020
, which is the screen color.
Only the brightness of said color matters (chrominance is encoded at the
PAL color carrier frequency, which is outside of the human hearing
range). There's no obvious relationship between the brightness of the C64 color
and its number, but that's fine - it actually makes the
waveforms more interesting.
Of course, the above uses up all four timers the C64 CIAs have, which means there
are no timers left for e.g. video stabilization, which is instead done
through the lightpen circuitry. (Finally! A use case for
$d013
. :))
Music is just one voice, but the song switches between voices (and
waveforms) often enough to sound mildly polyphonic.
How to drive video using an audio signal
The SID chip of the C64 internally operates (for PAL) at 9.85Mhz, and,
like the VIC, can be fed with new values at a rate of up to 246kHz.
The SID has a number of audio features. It can generate three voices
using multiple waveforms, it has an ADSR envelope generator, can sync
between voices, and apply filters.
Unfortunately, all this circuitry works at a (for video)
glacial pace: The highest frequency the chip can output is 3906Hz, which
is the equivalent of changing the video output every four rasterlines.
Similar with ADSR, for which the smallest possible configurable attack
time is 2 ms, so about 32 rasterlines.
But thankfully, there's also circuitry that is wired more directly and
and gives instant output: the volume register ($d418)!
This has been used in the past to generate samples at high frequencies
(16+ khz), and is a good choice for generating video, as well.
However, the C64 mainboard also, vexingly, passes the SID signal through
a analogue bandpass filter. And this always happens, regardless of
whether filtering is on or not.
This means that the pixels we work with are very wide, and also horizontally
blurred. Here's one "pixel", displayed on my 1084 monitor:
This blurryness poses an interesting constraint on effects. While technically,
you do have some degree of horizontal resolution, the blurriness makes it
unenticing to use it for scrollers. Here are a few letters, for illustration:
Signal Carnival makes heavy use of both axis,
but to cope with the bluriyness, the x axis is used for graphics elements that
are fine to blur, like e.g. textures.
Other than that, driving the video is just your normal vanilla video
bitbanging. Due to the bandpass filter, horizontal syncs (i.e., pulling
the signal line to ground) need to be precisely timed, so they get
recognized, but not mistaken for vertical syncs. (which differ from
horizontal syncs only in that the signal is pulled to ground a
little bit longer)
Video sync generation is happening at the same refresh frequency that
the VIC would have produced (so we can use raster interrupts and query
the lightpen), but we use a different horizontal frequency (64 cycles
per line instead of 63), since having that extra cycle proved useful
in a lot of effects. And besides, if you're generating your own
video signal, you might as well make your own rules!
Loading
I've written a new loader for probably every demo I've ever released on the C64,
and this one is no exception. Since a lot of the effects are quite
memory-hungry (we even play a sample at the end), loading breaks are
long enough that we can't just
pause audio while they happen
.
Hence, we have to bitbang audio the entire time. Also while transferring
data from the drive to the C64. Also during decrunching. (The
decruncher actually unrolls all copy loops, also for that reason)
The loader has a few gimmicks, like doing on-the-fly GCR decoding that
allows to write to any page (not just stack), and it buffers

data.title: Things Zig comptime won't do
data.author: JadedBlueEyes
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Zig语言中`comptime`功能的限制和独特设计。首先，`comptime`不会泄露主机信息，即使在交叉编译时，其行为也与运行时一致，不会访问编译主机架构。其次，Zig不支持通过任意字符串生成源代码，即没有类似`#eval`或动态代码生成的功能，而是通过部分求值和特化来实现类似效果。文章还展示了如何使用`comptime`实现类似代码生成的功能，如特化打印函数以处理不同数据类型，确保在编译时根据具体值进行部分求值和优化。Zig通过这种设计在保持表达力的同时引入了限制，确保编译时的行为可预测和一致。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言的comptime机制及其独特性

不同观点：
• [pron] 认为Zig的comptime机制通过结合替换其他语言中需要特化处理的特性以及引用透明性，提供了简单而强大的编程体验。这种设计在Scheme等Lisp语言中有类似之处，但Zig的实现方式不同，提供了独特的新颖性。
• [bunderbunder] 强调Zig的偏评估/特化功能可以覆盖大多数动态代码生成的用例，并通过部分应用和高级函数替代复杂的宏操作，体现了KISS原则。
• [ephaeton] 指出Zig的comptime存在一些缺点，社区通过使用zig build生成代码字符串来克服这些缺点。虽然这种方法有效，但感觉像是在用Perl和Tcl通过C传递字符串，不太理想。
• [pyrolistical] 强调comptime在实际使用中的灵活性，特别是在需要类型信息时，能够轻松添加并传递到上层函数。
• [karmakaze] 质疑Zig的comptime功能的独特性，认为其他语言也有类似的编译时评估能力，并询问具体是哪些语言。
• [no_wizard] 表示对Zig语言和工具的喜爱，但希望有类似于Rust的安全模式，认为这是与Rust相比的一个权衡。
• [paldepind2] 认为Zig的comptime功能非常强大，能够在编译时表示类型为值，且没有运行时开销，也不需要像Lisp的宏或Rust的过程宏那样复杂。
• [forrestthewoods] 对comptime代码在编译时的执行位置感到困惑，特别是跨平台编译时，主机平台和目标平台的差异及其隐藏机制让他感到不解。

补充讨论：
• Zig的comptime机制的独特性及其在语言中的位置是讨论的一个核心点，有人认为这是一种新颖的设计，而有人则对其限制和复杂性提出了质疑。
• 社区对Zig的comptime功能在实际应用中的表现有不同的看法，有些人赞赏其简化代码的能力，而另一些人则对其不足之处提出了批评。
• 跨平台编译时的comptime行为和主机平台与目标平台的关系引起了讨论者的困惑，说明这是一个值得进一步澄清的技术细节。

争议焦点：
• Zig的comptime功能是否真的如宣传的那样独特和强大，还是存在一些限制和不足。
• 跨平台编译时comptime代码的执行细节及其对主机平台和目标平台的处理方式。

通过这些观点和讨论，可以看出Zig的comptime机制在提供强大编译时能力的同时，也带来了一些复杂性和争议。

43744591.article_content:
Things Zig comptime Won’t Do
Apr 19, 2025
Es el disco de Odín. Tiene un solo lado. En la tierra no hay otra
cosa que tenga un solo lado.
Zig’s comptime feature is most famous for what it can do: generics!,
conditional compilation
!,
subtyping
!, serialization!,
ORM
! That’s fascinating, but, to be fair, there’s a bunch of
languages with quite powerful compile time evaluation capabilities
that can do equivalent things. What I find more interesting is that
Zig comptime is actually quite restrictive, by design, and won’t do
many things! It manages to be very expressive
despite
being
pretty limited. Let’s see!
No Host Leakage
When you execute code at compile time, on which machine does it
execute? The natural answer is “on your machine”, but it is wrong!
The code might not run on your machine, it can be cross compiled!
For overall development sanity, it is important that
comptime
code observes the same behavior as the runtime
code, and doesn’t leak details about the host on which the code is
compiled. Zig doesn’t give comptime code access to host architecture
(host — machine on which you compile code). Consider this Zig
program:
const
std =
@import
(
"std"
);
comptime
{
const
x:
usize
=
0xbeef
;
const
xs: []
const
u8
= std.mem.asBytes(
&
x);
for
(xs)
|
byte
|
{
@compileLog
(byte);
}
}
I get the following output when compiling normally, on my computer
for my computer:
λ ~/zig-0.14/zig build-lib main.zig
@as(u8, 239)
@as(u8, 190)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
But if I cross compile to a 32 bit big-endian architecture, comptime
observes correct
usize
:
λ ~/zig-0.14/zig build-lib -target thumbeb-freestanding-none main.zig
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 0)
@as(u8, 190)
@as(u8, 239)
My understanding is that Jai, for example, doesn’t do this, and runs
comptime code on the host.
Rust’s declarative macros and const-fn don’t observe host
architecture, but procedural macros do.
No #eval
Many powerful compile-time meta programming systems work by allowing
you to inject arbitrary strings into compilation, sort of like
#include
whose argument is a shell-script that generates the
text to include dynamically. For example, D mixins work that way:
https://dlang.org/articles/mixin.html
And Rust macros, while technically producing a token-tree rather
than a string, are more or less the same. In contrast, there’s
absolutely no facility for dynamic source code generation in Zig.
You just can’t do that, the feature isn’t!
Zig has a completely different feature, partial
evaluation/specialization, which, none the less, is enough to cover
most of use-cases for dynamic code generation. Let’s see an
artificial example:
fn
f
(x:
u32
, y:
u32
)
u32
{
if
(x
==
0
)
return
y
+
1
;
if
(x
==
1
)
return
y
*
2
;
return
y;
}
This is a normal function that dispatches on the first argument to
select an operation to apply to the second argument. Nothing fancy!
Now, the single feature that Zig has is marking the first argument
with
comptime
fn
f
(
comptime
x:
u32
, y:
u32
)
u32
{
if
(x
==
0
)
return
y
+
1
;
if
(x
==
1
)
return
y
*
2
;
return
y;
}
The restriction here is that now, of course, when you call
f
, the first argument must be comptime-known. You can
f(92, user_input())
,
but you can’t
f(user_input(), 92)
.
The carrot you’ll get in exchange is a guarantee that, for each
specific call with a particular value of
x
, the
compiler will partially evaluate
f
, so only one branch
will be left.
Zig is an imperative language. Not everything is a function, there’s
also control flow expressions, and they include partially-evaluated
variations. For example,
for(xs)
is a normal runtime
for loop over a slice,
comptime for(xs)
evaluates the
entire loop at compile time, requiring that
xs
is
comptime-known, and
inline for(xs)
requires that just
the length of
xs
is known at comptime.
Let’s apply specialization to the classic problem solved by
code-generation — printing. You can imagine a proc-macro style
solution that prints a struct by reflecting on which fields it has
and emitting the code to print each field.
In Zig, the same is achieved by specializing a recursive
print
function on the value of type:

S =
struct
{
int:
u32
,
string: []
const
u8
,
nested:
struct
{
int:
u32
,
},
};
pub
fn
main
()
void
{
const
s: S = .{
.int =
1
,
.string =
"hello"
,
.nested = .{ .int =
2
},
};
print(S, s);
}
fn
print
(
comptime
T:
type
, value: T)
void
{

(T
==
u32
)
return
print_u32(value);

(T
==
[]

u8
)
return
print_string(value);

@typeInfo

data.author: greenie_beans

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对旧金山当前情况及其成因的不同看法，以及对科技公司和城市治理的批评与辩护

不同观点：
• **[mgraczyk的观点]**：认为关于旧金山的负面故事往往忽视了实际情况。他指出，旧金山的犯罪率和无家可归者数量已经下降，这些改善源于政府运作效率的提升，并且一些富人主动出资解决问题。他还质疑将警察、消防员的高薪与科技工作者对比是否公平，并指出旧金山已经是高税城市，进一步加税未必有效。

• **[buss的观点]**：作为GrowSF的联合创始人，他反驳文章中将GrowSF描述为秘密阴谋的一部分。他认为GrowSF关注实际成果，而不是政治姿态或进步主义修辞。

• **[TulliusCicero的观点]**：通过数据指出旧金山人均预算远高于类似城市，但公共服务仍显资金不足，暗示城市管理存在问题。他还提到旧金山在无家可归者问题上的高额支出与未解决的现状，批评所谓“进步”管理的失败。

• **[almost_usual的观点]**：从个人经历出发，指出旧金山的科技繁荣在十年前已经存在，COVID和远程工作对城市经济的冲击已经显现。

• **[jaredsmithse的观点]**：讽刺文章中提到的广告牌事件，认为对大公司贪婪的指责过于简单化。

• **[jgalt212的观点]**：将旧金山与曾经的底特律对比，警示如果不加管理，旧金山可能面临类似的衰落。

• **[kjellsbells的观点]**：从历史角度分析，认为富人和有权势者推动城市变革的热情并不新鲜，并将这种现象与历史上其他时期的扩张主义和乌托邦思想相比较，认为这是傲慢的表现。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于旧金山城市问题的成因和解决方案。一方认为科技公司和富人干预是问题根源，另一方则认为正是这些富人和有效政府行动改善了城市状况。
• 讨论还涉及旧金山高预算与公共服务不足的矛盾，暗示城市管理可能存在深层次问题。
• 科技公司在城市发展中的角色和影响也被广泛讨论，特别是在住房和公共服务方面的贡献和责任。

这些观点共同描绘了对旧金山现状的不同解读，以及对城市未来发展的不同期望。

• **[mgraczyk的观点]**：认为关于旧金山的负面故事往往忽视了实际情况。他指出，旧金山的犯罪率和无家可归者数量已经下降，这些改善源于政府运作效率的提升，并且一些富人主动出资解决问题。他还质疑将警察、消防员的高薪与科技工作者对比是否公平，并指出旧金山已经是高税城市，进一步加税未必有效。

• **[buss的观点]**：作为GrowSF的联合创始人，他反驳文章中将GrowSF描述为秘密阴谋的一部分。他认为GrowSF关注实际成果，而不是政治姿态或进步主义修辞。

• **[TulliusCicero的观点]**：通过数据指出旧金山人均预算远高于类似城市，但公共服务仍显资金不足，暗示城市管理存在问题。他还提到旧金山在无家可归者问题上的高额支出与未解决的现状，批评所谓“进步”管理的失败。

• **[almost_usual的观点]**：从个人经历出发，指出旧金山的科技繁荣在十年前已经存在，COVID和远程工作对城市经济的冲击已经显现。

• **[jaredsmithse的观点]**：讽刺文章中提到的广告牌事件，认为对大公司贪婪的指责过于简单化。

• **[jgalt212的观点]**：将旧金山与曾经的底特律对比，警示如果不加管理，旧金山可能面临类似的衰落。

• **[kjellsbells的观点]**：从历史角度分析，认为富人和有权势者推动城市变革的热情并不新鲜，并将这种现象与历史上其他时期的扩张主义和乌托邦思想相比较，认为这是傲慢的表现。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于旧金山城市问题的成因和解决方案。一方认为科技公司和富人干预是问题根源，另一方则认为正是这些富人和有效政府行动改善了城市状况。
• 讨论还涉及旧金山高预算与公共服务不足的矛盾，暗示城市管理可能存在深层次问题。
• 科技公司在城市发展中的角色和影响也被广泛讨论，特别是在住房和公共服务方面的贡献和责任。

这些观点共同描绘了对旧金山现状的不同解读，以及对城市未来发展的不同期望。

data.title: The movie mistake mystery from "Revenge of the Sith"
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了电影中一些不易察觉的“穿帮”镜头，这些镜头虽然打破了电影的幻觉，但对影迷而言却是令人兴奋的发现。作者特别喜欢那些隐藏在明显之处、多次观看才能注意到的错误，认为这些瞬间揭示了电影制作的巧妙工艺。文章列举了几个经典例子，如《光荣》（1989）中现代手表的出现，《好家伙》（1990）中车牌掉落的场景，《异形2》（1986）中机器人Bishop的“分身”技巧，以及《大白鲨》（1971）和《教父》（1972）中工作人员在反射中意外入镜的瞬间。作者认为，这些穿帮镜头虽然打破了电影的幻觉，但对热爱电影制作过程的观众来说，是令人愉悦的提醒，展示了电影背后的魔法技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电影修复中是否应该修正错误

不同观点：
• crazygringo：认为修复中修正错误是一种历史修正主义，尤其是在修正没有导演意图的错误时。他区分了修正小失误（如车牌或手表）和更换音乐、CG特效等重大改动，认为前者可以接受，后者改变了艺术的本质。
• dfxm12：认为电影既是艺术也是商品，修正错误是可以接受的，尤其是当导演或演员不在意时。他还提到其他艺术形式（如小说、版画）也会有修订版。
• sickcodebruh：从粉丝和创作者的双重角度出发，作为粉丝喜欢小错误，因为它们让人感受到作品的人性化；但作为创作者，会尽力修正错误以避免分心。
• haunter：更讨厌剪辑错误，如《飞行家》中的剪辑不连贯，认为这些错误更影响观影体验。
• pavlov：强调演员在绿幕前表演的挑战，认为依赖实际场景和特效的电影（如《哈利波特》）比完全依赖数字特效的（如《星球大战》）更耐看。
• _wire_：提到自己注意到《角斗士》和《夺宝奇兵》中的小错误，认为这些错误一旦被发现就难以忽略，但同时也增加了电影的艺术性。
• p_ing：将电影错误的修正与小说的修订相比较，认为为了故事的清晰性进行修正并没有错。
• mproud：与p_ing观点相似，认为电影错误的修正类似于文学作者在再版时修正错误。

补充讨论：
• strunz：对《现代启示录》中意外出现在电影中的无名人物更感兴趣，想知道其背景和想法。
• gorfian_robot：提到《星球大战》电影的“去特殊版”编辑，为有兴趣的人提供了参考。
• nickvec：指出在文章中过早地将安纳金称为达斯·维达可能引起混淆。
• vmilner：提到在《终结者》4K版中发现的新错误。
• _wire_：还提到《The Party》中的一个幽默场景，可能与《Glory》中的手表错误有关。

争议焦点：
• 修正电影错误是否属于历史修正主义，是否改变了电影的原有意图和艺术性。
• 电影作为商品和艺术的双重属性，使得修正错误在不同情况下有不同的合理性。

43745141.article_content:
Movies are handmade, and just like any other art form, sometimes the seams that hold movies together become visible to the audience. For movie fans, these moments are very exciting. Catching a glimpse behind the scenes is an exhilarating experience. My favorite kind of “movie mistake” is the kind that is hiding in plain sight... but the casual viewer missed it upon first viewing. Or perhaps even the second viewing, or even the third.
I’m particularly obsessed with moments that reveal the craft and artistry of the magic trick of a shot that slightly shatters the illusion of cinema. These revealing moments have been in movies since the dawn of cinema, and are everywhere (if you know exactly where to look).
•  •  •  •
One of my favorite films of all time also has one of the funniest revealing mistakes I've seen. Edward Zwick's "Glory" (1989) takes place during the American Civil War, and this scene has a blink-and-you'll-miss-it reminder of the film's very modern production:
"Glory" (1989)
Because the audiences' eyes are firmly fixed on Morgan Freeman's character in the center of frame, very few will ever pick up the little kid with the extremely modern wristwatch that enters frame on far screen right. Sometimes the on-set teams that work with featured extras—as well as the costume department that dress the extras—will occasionally miss a modern piece of jewelry on an actor.
Here's a fun one from Martin Scorsese's masterpiece "Goodfellas" (1990), in one of the closing shots of a nail-bitingly tense scene where Karen nearly walks into an ambush:
"Goodfellas" (1990)
The period-appropriate "movie" license plate dramatically dangles then completely falls off the car in the middle of the take, revealing the actual 1990-era license plate of the car used for the scene. This is an accidental and hilarious glimpse into the detailed hard work that goes into making a Hollywood period piece (this portion of the film takes place in 1980), where every license plate of every car in the movie needed special, detailed work to make them period-appropriate.
The finale of James Cameron's epic "Aliens" (1986) features the android Bishop (Lance Henriksen) getting severed in half, but still functioning enough to save Newt (Carrie Henn) from getting sucked into the vacuum of space. The action-packed scene features an absolutely wonderful accidental reveal of how the cut-in-half android was accomplished on the set:
"Aliens" (1986)
The amazing makeup effects applied to Henriksen's body covers the bottom half of his body which is hidden through a hole in the set. But in order to get that little bit of extra athletic stretch to grab Newt, Henriksen popped his body out of the hole a little too far, revealing the classic stage trick. However, I'd gather that 99% of the audience has never noticed this little reveal of stagecraft since our eyes are fixed on Newt on screen right, sliding toward the airlock, and not on the ground contact of Bishop's half-body, which had already been firmly established in the scene.
Avoiding reflections of the crew appearing to camera is a constant struggle for filmmakers. In Steven Spielberg's first masterpiece "Duel" (1971), David (Dennis Weaver) gets into a phone booth to make a call, with the front glass face of the booth aimed directly at the camera, and if the audience's gaze drifted off of Weaver's face, they could catch a glimpse of the crew:
"Duel" (1971)
In the reflection, we see a few crew members on screen left, the camera itself, and director Spielberg on the right (he's the one shuffling left and right, who lowers his head in the middle of the take). Again, like all the examples I'm providing in this article, hardly anyone would ever notice these moments. When a viewer catches these brief moments, the illusion of the movie is briefly broken, but for fans of the filmmaking process, it's a joyful reminder of the overall magic trick. The most intimate movie scene with only two characters in a desolate, isolated environment actually was created by dozens and dozens of crew members standing slightly out of frame.
Look for another accidental 'crew caught on camera' moment in the reflection in a car window in the 'leave the gun, take the cannoli' scene from "The Godfather" (1972), one that very few people ever notice.
Here's a super quick revealing mistake from "The Dark Knight" (2008) that is a true "you'll never see this in real time" moment:
"The Dark Knight" (2008)
Although "The Dark Knight" example gives the audience a much clearer look at the camera operator, the focus puller(?) and the camera itself reflected in the interrogation room’s mirrors, the shot is a lot harder to see the crew members and equipment in real time due to the chaotic and energetic camera movement, as opposed to the locked off nature of the "Duel" example.

data.title: The Joy of Linux Theming in the Age of Bootable Containers
data.author: dopple
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了在Linux桌面环境中进行主题定制和配置的演变，特别是在可启动容器时代下的乐趣与挑战。作者回顾了过去几十年在Xfce、LXQt等桌面环境中进行自定义的经历，包括使用Shell脚本和Ansible playbooks来记录和自动化配置过程。然而，这些方法常导致系统组件损坏或不稳定。

文章重点介绍了**bootc项目**，一种通过容器定义操作系统的工具，允许用户在容器中定制和测试桌面主题，并通过重启快速切换或回滚。这种方法提供了高度的灵活性和安全性，解决了传统方式中的配置漂移问题。

作者还探讨了其他实现类似效果的方法，如使用systemd-sysext或Nix，但认为这些方法在灵活性和可靠性上不如bootc。最后，文章反思了创建新Linux发行版的必要性，尤其是为简单的主题定制而新建发行版是否值得。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用容器技术测试和分发Linux配置（dotfiles）的优缺点，以及容器技术在Linux桌面环境和主题定制中的应用。

不同观点：
• **支持使用容器技术**：
   - **nickjj**：认为容器技术（如Docker）非常适合测试dotfiles，可以在短时间内完成端到端测试，且无需修改主机系统。容器还可以通过卷挂载保持运行，方便增量测试。
   - **sohrob**：认为像bootc这样的项目是Linux当前最令人兴奋的进展之一，能够提供比现有方式更稳定的解决方案，并希望Debian等项目采用这种容器化的工作流。

• **对供应链安全的担忧**：
   - **kayson**：对容器文件中使用多个第三方仓库表示担忧，认为存在供应链安全风险，特别是在版本未锁定的情况下。相比之下，Debian等传统发行版的包管理更值得信赖。

• **对主题定制的讨论**：
   - **OsrsNeedsf2P**：质疑为什么Linux主题定制没有更广泛的热情，提到了Chicago95和Garuda Linux等项目，指出目前主题定制网站和工具的不足。
   - **qwerty456127**：对现代操作系统的主题定制能力表示失望，期望有一个繁荣的主题定制社区。

• **其他技术选择的讨论**：
   - **Havoc**：更倾向于使用LXC而非Docker，并认为窗口管理器的类型（如平铺窗口管理器）对用户体验影响更大。
   - **undeniablemess**：提到NixOS的impermanence模块，认为其无状态特性与容器技术有相似之处。
   - **dicytea**：认为bootc在图形化虚拟机中的一键启动方法不够完善，需要手动构建镜像和配置qemu。

• **对资源浪费的质疑**：
   - **WesolyKubeczek**：认为为了放置几个文件而打包整个OCI镜像是浪费资源，建议学习RPM打包并使用COPR仓库，将OCI和bootc作为可选方案。

• **其他意见**：
   - **mfro**：提到Blue95项目，并表示更希望有一种可以轻松安装在基础系统上的解决方案。
   - **trollied**：回忆Enlightenment桌面环境，认为其在X11时代的创新尝试令人怀念。
   - **gigel82**：对文章网站的CSS样式表示不满，认为其对OLED屏幕不友好。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：容器技术在Linux桌面环境和主题定制中的适用性及安全性。支持者认为容器提供了快速测试和隔离环境的优势，而反对者则担心供应链安全和资源浪费问题。
- **其他技术**：讨论中还提到了ZFS快照、NixOS的impermanence模块和LXC等其他技术方案，显示出对多种解决方案的开放态度。
- **主题定制社区**：部分评论对Linux主题定制社区的现状表示不满，认为缺乏完善的工具和社区支持。

43743784.article_content:
The Joy of Linux Theming in the Age of Bootable Containers
2025-04-20
@ledif
What is a Linux distribution anyway?
Having spent a couple of decades in the Linux world, I have always had an interest in Linux desktop environments and how they are themed.
I would often come across a post on
/r/unixporn
that inspired me to try to customize the look and feel of my desktop environment. So I would install Xfce, LXQt or Sway and try to recreate components that I like from other users or create my own. I would end up installing different kinds of panels, plugins, docks and launchers as well as random themes, fonts and sounds.
A portion of this process would be documented, initially as random shell scripts in my home directory, before graduating to Ansible playbooks – with a brief detour into Nix that I will not elaborate on. Some of the customizations would live in my home directory, but there were often system-wide modifications to
/usr
required.
Eventually, the constant churn and randomly broken desktop components such as a panel that mysteriously vanished or a non-functional dock led me to stick with the stock configuration of whatever desktop environment I was using at the time.
The major desktop environments,
KDE Plasma
and
GNOME
, are both well polished and great out of the box. The desktop experience that they have delivered over the last few years has contributed to desktop Linux being the best it has ever been, in my opinion.
But the itch to customize and tweak my desktop environment in fun and interesting ways is still there. Eventually, I was introduced to the concept of bootable containers.
Bootc As A Themer’s Playground
⌗
The
bootc
project, originally developed by
Red Hat
but now part of the
Cloud Native Computing Foundation
, is a core component of the
Bootable Containers Initiative
. Conceptually, it allows you to define your operating system as a Containerfile:
FROM quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:42
RUN dnf install -y my-custom-theme my-custom-fonts my-custom-panel
Once written, you can build the container locally and instruct your bootc-aware system to use the new image.
sudo podman build -f Containerfile -t my-fedora
sudo bootc switch --transport containers-storage localhost/my-fedora:latest
After a reboot, the system’s deployment is defined by the new container.
With Fedora Atomic systems,
/usr
is mounted read-only and because your operating system is defined by an OCI container, it is incredibly easy to revert to a previous tag of that container. I can easily create a throwaway container where I test out ideas for a theme, reboot into the new deployment and test it out on bare-metal. I can roll back to the previous container if necessary or create a new container with follow-up modifications.
One downside is that this reboot-heavy workflow can obviously cause some friction. This can be mitigated somewhat by enabling “Development Mode” with
ostree admin unlock
, which creates a temporary writable overlayfs on top of
/usr
. I often find myself using this mode to temporarily install some package, theme or configuration in
/usr
. After verifying that it works as expected, I can add that functionality to the Containerfile. If it doesn’t work, I can either reboot to get rid of the changes, or (more likely) just forget about the change and it will remove itself whenever I reboot normally. The lack of cruft that accumulates over time in a typical Linux installation is one of the major advantages of this approach.
Of course, there are other ways to achieve similar results without using a bootable container model:
You can write shell scripts or Ansible playbooks and hope that they accurately capture changes to the system so that they can be reliably undone. Typically, configuration drift that occurs as software gets updated is not addressed.
With
systemd-sysext(8)
, you can create a squashfs image of a filesystem containing your theming changes for
/usr
and overlay it on top of the root filesystem. An ecosystem around how these images should be created, maintained, deployed and updated has yet to emerge.
You can inscribe your custom theming as runes in an arcane and inscrutable functional language known only to the elders as N̸̘̏͑̕͝į̸̈́̂x̸͙̑̅̒.
In my opinion, none of the alternatives provide the same level of flexibility and tooling support as writing a Dockerfile, nor can they achieve bootc’s level of safety and reliability by making it extremely difficult to bork your
/usr
directory. And if the
/usr
directory somehow gets borked anyway, rolling back to the previously deployed container is just a reboot away.
What Is A Distro?
⌗
BlueXP
Blue9
A few weeks ago, an OCI image based on Fedora Xfce Atomic that I made called
Blue95
was posted to
Hacker News
. For the most part, the reception was warm but there were some interesting questions that were raised, such as:
Is it really necessary to spin up an entirely new distro for an XFCE+GTK theme?

文章讨论了在Linux桌面环境中进行主题定制和配置的演变，特别是在可启动容器时代下的乐趣与挑战。作者回顾了过去几十年在Xfce、LXQt等桌面环境中进行自定义的经历，包括使用Shell脚本和Ansible playbooks来记录和自动化配置过程。然而，这些方法常导致系统组件损坏或不稳定。

文章重点介绍了**bootc项目**，一种通过容器定义操作系统的工具，允许用户在容器中定制和测试桌面主题，并通过重启快速切换或回滚。这种方法提供了高度的灵活性和安全性，解决了传统方式中的配置漂移问题。

作者还探讨了其他实现类似效果的方法，如使用systemd-sysext或Nix，但认为这些方法在灵活性和可靠性上不如bootc。最后，文章反思了创建新Linux发行版的必要性，尤其是为简单的主题定制而新建发行版是否值得。

不同观点：
• **支持使用容器技术**：

   - **sohrob**：认为像bootc这样的项目是Linux当前最令人兴奋的进展之一，能够提供比现有方式更稳定的解决方案，并希望Debian等项目采用这种容器化的工作流。

data.title: OAuth's Role in MCP Security
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Microservice Context Propagation）和OAuth 2.0协议的安全性、应用及其在授权和认证中的角色。

不同观点：
• [lsaferite] 认为MCP服务器如果是自建或由API提供方控制，风险类似于浏览器或其他本地软件泄露访问令牌。只有使用第三方托管的MCP服务器时，才额外增加了令牌暴露的风险。他还指出，目前许多参与MCP的人缺乏对相关风险的了解，尤其是在信任边界和数据泄露方面。他特别关注MCP服务器在处理敏感数据时的安全性，并认为当前缺乏有效的方法来防止数据泄露。

• [korginator] 指出OAuth 2.0是一个授权协议，而不是身份层或认证协议。他认为文章将OAuth与认证类型、钓鱼攻击等混为一谈是不准确的。他强调行业已经有广泛使用的方案（如OAuth+OIDC），并批评文章的最后两段没有实质内容且不够严谨。

• [gsibble] 认为MCP与OAuth的集成非常困难，提出诸如回调URL的选择以及如何在不将令牌存储在LLM（可能指大语言模型）提供商的情况下传递令牌等问题。他质疑文章的价值，认为其没有很好地解决实际的技术难题。

补充讨论：
• [lsaferite] 特别关注MCP在实际应用中的风险，尤其是由于用户对MCP的理解不足导致的不当信任边界设置。
• [korginator] 强调了OAuth 2.0的纯粹授权性质，并指出文章在讨论范围上的不准确性。
• [gsibble] 提出了MCP与OAuth集成时面临的具体技术挑战，如回调和令牌存储问题。

争议焦点：
• MCP服务器托管位置（自建、API提供方、第三方）对令牌泄露风险的影响。
• OAuth 2.0在文章中被赋予的过多角色（授权、认证、防钓鱼等），导致对其功能和适用范围的混淆。
• MCP与OAuth集成时的实际技术难题，如回调URL和令牌存储问题。

data.title: Pushing the Limits of LLM Quantization via the Linearity Theorem
data.author: felineflock
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种通过"线性定理"推动大语言模型量化极限的方法。该定理建立了层间$\ell_2$重建误差与模型困惑度增加之间的直接关系。基于此，文章提出了两种新应用：（1）一种无需数据的大语言模型量化方法HIGGS，利用Hadamard旋转和最小均方误差最优网格，优于以往所有无需数据的方法；（2）在给定压缩约束下，通过动态规划找到非均匀每层量化级别的最优解。实验证明，该方法在Llama-3.1、Llama-3.2及Qwen系列模型上实现了更好的精度-压缩权衡，并能在各种批量大小下通过GPU内核高效支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）量化方法的理论突破与实际效果

不同观点：
• Scene_Cast2认为，基于目前对LLM工作原理的理解（如Anthropic的研究），可以利用这些 insights 来更好地进行量化。他特别提到，LLMs通过若干神经元的旋转（而非幅度）来编码概念，并将此与最近的LLM可解释性研究联系起来，暗示这些理论可以帮助改进量化方法。

• cs702对文章的质量表示肯定，但指出该文章并非轻松易读。他提到作者声称取得了一些理论突破，包括：无数据LLM量化方法，据称该方法在性能上优于以往所有无数据方法，包括NF4；以及在"中等比特宽度"范围内，找到与给定压缩约束相匹配的非均匀每层量化水平的最佳方法。他还提到，文章展示了在流行LLM上改进的准确性-压缩权衡。

补充讨论：
• Scene_Cast2的观点更多是从理论角度出发，结合现有的LLM可解释性研究，探讨如何将相关理论应用于LLM量化。
• cs702则更关注文章的实际应用和效果，特别是作者所声称的理论突破在实际应用中的表现，以及文章的易读性和技术贡献。
• 争议的焦点可能在于该文章所声称的理论突破是否如其所述在实际应用中具有显著优势，以及这些方法是否能被广泛应用和验证。

Title:
Pushing the Limits of Large Language Model Quantization via the Linearity Theorem
Authors:
Vladimir Malinovskii
,
Andrei Panferov
,
Ivan Ilin
,
Han Guo
,
Peter Richtárik
,
Dan Alistarh
View a PDF of the paper titled Pushing the Limits of Large Language Model Quantization via the Linearity Theorem, by Vladimir Malinovskii and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Quantizing large language models has become a standard way to reduce their memory and computational costs. Typically, existing methods focus on breaking down the problem into individual layer-wise sub-problems, and minimizing per-layer error, measured via various metrics. Yet, this approach currently lacks theoretical justification and the metrics employed may be sub-optimal. In this paper, we present a "linearity theorem" establishing a direct relationship between the layer-wise $\ell_2$ reconstruction error and the model perplexity increase due to quantization. This insight enables two novel applications: (1) a simple data-free LLM quantization method using Hadamard rotations and MSE-optimal grids, dubbed HIGGS, which outperforms all prior data-free approaches such as the extremely popular NF4 quantized format, and (2) an optimal solution to the problem of finding non-uniform per-layer quantization levels which match a given compression constraint in the medium-bitwidth regime, obtained by reduction to dynamic programming. On the practical side, we demonstrate improved accuracy-compression trade-offs on Llama-3.1 and 3.2-family models, as well as on Qwen-family models. Further, we show that our method can be efficiently supported in terms of GPU kernels at various batch sizes, advancing both data-free and non-uniform quantization for LLMs.

data.title: Crows can recognize geometric regularity
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 德国图宾根大学的研究人员发现，乌鸦能够识别几何规律。在发表于《Science Advances》期刊的研究中，Philipp Schmidbauer、Madita Hahn和Andreas Nieder通过实验测试了乌鸦识别几何形状的能力。实验中，乌鸦需要从一组刺激物中啄出不同的形状，选对可获得食物奖励。实验显示，乌鸦能识别出如星星与月亮、非对称四边形与对称四边形等不同形状。即使面对细微差异，乌鸦的准确率也高于随机选择。研究表明，乌鸦具备一定的几何规律识别能力，且无需事先学习。这一发现暗示其他动物也可能具备类似能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：动物的智力及其与人类智力的比较

不同观点：
• CountWSS认为，认为“只有人类能够识别形状”这一观点已经过时，类似于“科学证实动物会感到疼痛”的发现。这表明动物的智力可能被低估。
• Terretta引用Adrian Tchaikovsky的小说《Children of Memory》中的乌鸦智能为例，探讨“什么是智力”的问题，并通过熟悉的例子来定义可能过于陌生的概念。
• Sayamqazi分享个人经历，表示山羊能够通过嘴巴旋转门栓手柄并打开门，说明动物的问题解决能力常被低估。
• Djmips描述观察到乌鸦在水中软化人类丢弃的食物以便食用，显示乌鸦的创造性行为。

补充讨论：
• Worldsayshi提问乌鸦、海豚、章鱼和非人类猿类的智力如何比较，是否存在巨大的智力差距，以及这种差距是否可以量化。
• Almosthere简单指出乌鸦可以从300英尺外识别出虫子，表明其识别能力。
• SwtCyber提到乌鸦在视觉任务中的表现下降但仍高于随机选择，表明它们可能在“思考”而不仅仅是反应。
• Wglb提供了一篇Science Advances论文链接，为讨论提供科学依据。
• Cdplayer96幽默地询问训练乌鸦收集城市中散落的硬币是否合法。
• Alexfromapex分享个人观察，表示乌鸦能够识别他何时在草坪上播种草籽。
• 1337biz提到有一群人训练野生乌鸦做各种事情，显示乌鸦的聪明才智。
• Domofutu提供了一个相关讨论的链接。
• NanoYohaneTSU讽刺地说训练动物做事情是可以的，质疑这是否已成为媒体报道的大新闻。
• Andoando认为狗和其他有眼睛的动物也能做到，只是兴趣和学习动机的差异。
• Metalman详细描述了乌鸦在建筑物和公路边有条理地觅食的行为，显示其高度的认知能力。

争议焦点：
• 动物智力的比较及其与人类智力的关系是讨论的核心，特别是不同物种间的智力差异是否可以量化，以及如何定义和衡量这种智力。

Crows can recognize geometric regularity
by Bob Yirka										 										 , Phys.org
Intruder detection task. Two carrion crows were trained to detect an intruder stimulus in an array of six simultaneously presented stimuli. The crows initiated the trial by moving their head in front of the screen whenever a go-stimulus appeared. After a prestimulus period of 200 ms, an array of six stimuli was displayed. The crows responded by pecking on the intruder. In 50% of the trials, the crows were tested with non-quadrilateral background stimuli (top); in this example, the crescent is the intruder among stars. In the other 50% of the trials, the crows were tested with quadrilateral probe stimuli (bottom); in this example, a nonsymmetric quadrilateral is the intruder among symmetric quadrilaterals. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718
A trio of animal physiologists at the University of Tübingen, in Germany, has found that at least one species of crow has the ability to recognize geometric regularity. In their
study
published in the journal
Science Advances
, Philipp Schmidbauer, Madita Hahn and Andreas Nieder conducted several experiments that involved testing crows on their ability to recognize geometric shapes.
Recognizing regularity in geometric shapes means being able to pick out one
shape
that is different from others in a group—picking out a plastic star, for example, when it is placed among several plastic moons. Testing for the ability to recognize geometric regularity has been done with many animals, including chimps and bonobos. Until now, this ability has never been observed in any creature except for humans.
Because of that, the team started with a bit of skepticism when they began testing carrion crows. In their work, the testing was done using computer screens—the birds were asked to peck the outlier in a group; if they chose correctly, they got a food treat. The team chose to test carrion crows because prior experiments have shown them to have exceptional intelligence and mathematical capabilities.
All the birds tested caught on right away. Each could pick out a star if it was placed within a group of rectangles, for example. To determine their level of skill, the researchers started showing them objects that were only slightly different: one box that was tilted slightly, for example, among others that were not. Their accuracy went down, but it was still much higher than chance.
Example of a canonical probe stimulus layout. Here, a deviant shape (in the top-left position) was placed amid five right hinge reference shapes and had to be recognized as the intruder. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718
Continued testing showed that the birds had some understanding of right angles, parallel lines and even some degree of symmetry.
The research team suggests their experiments were quite convincing—the crows were very obviously able to recognize geometric regularity. They note that the experiments also showed that the
birds
could do so with no prior learning. The findings strongly suggest that the ability exists in other animals as well.
(A) Test stimulus set. The crows were tested with a stimulus set consisting of five pairs of nonquadrilateral shapes used as familiar background stimuli that had been used during training (left) and five pairs of quadrilateral shapes used as probe stimuli (right). (B) The five quadrilateral reference shapes used to test deviation from geometric regularity. From left to right, the quadrilaterals increasingly differed in geometric properties (parallelism, symmetry, perpendicularity, equal sides, and equal angles). Here, they are ordered from left to right by decreasing regularity. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adt3718

data.title: TikZJax: Embedding LaTeX Drawings in HTML
data.author: steventhedev
data.article_summary: TikZJax 是一个将 TikZ 代码转换为 SVG 的工具。通过在 HTML 文档的 `<head>` 中引入相关 CSS 和 JS 文件，并在 `<body>` 中使用 `<script type="text/tikz">` 标签嵌入 TikZ 代码，浏览器会将该代码编译为 SVG 图形。例如，简单的圆和交换图代码都能被渲染为对应的 SVG。其工作原理是利用 WebAssembly 将 TeX 编译为 Web 可用的格式，通过 PGF 驱动和 dvi2html 将 DVI 输出转换为 SVG，整个过程在浏览器中完成。详细示例和演示可访问 [https://tikzjax.com/](https://tikzjax.com/)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕TikZJax及其在浏览器中实现LaTeX/TikZ渲染的讨论，涉及技术实现、优缺点以及使用体验。

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏] ics对Jim Fowler及其Calculus视频的推荐，认为其风格生动有趣，适合复习和学习。同时对TikZJax的实现表示赞赏，认为这种技术破解很有趣。
• [优缺点分析] apetresc对TikZJax的整体印象积极，但指出了多个问题，包括某些核心库功能未实现或出错，存在长期未修复的bug，以及开发者缺乏维护。他还提到构建过程复杂，但仍认为TikZ是最好的图表制作工具之一。
• [技术细节讨论] frumplestlatz对使用“core dump”作为优化手段表示兴趣，并提到了其在其他项目（如Emacs）中的历史先例，同时对在WebAssembly中实现这一方法表示好奇。
• [服务器端渲染偏好] ycombinatrix表示更倾向于在服务器端进行SVG渲染，而非在客户端，暗示对客户端渲染的性能或实用性有所保留。
• [静态SVG生成] xenonite认为生成静态SVG并嵌入静态网页生成器可能更符合一般需求，提供了一个相关技术文章链接。
• [移动端体验] Garlef提到该技术在移动端表现不佳，暗示其在移动设备上的兼容性或性能可能存在问题。
• [怀旧评论] klabetron对Jim Fowler及其在高中介绍的LaTeX表示怀念，个人情感较强，未深入讨论技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要集中在TikZJax的实现细节和实用性上，尤其是功能缺失、bug未修复以及构建过程复杂等问题。
• 对渲染方式的偏好有所不同，部分用户倾向于服务器端渲染，部分用户则认为静态SVG生成更实用。
• 移动端体验和兼容性也被提及，但未深入讨论。

TikZJax
TikZJax converts
script
tags (containing TikZ code) into SVGs.
See a live demo at
https://tikzjax.com/
.
Example
In the
<head>
of your HTML, include
<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="https://tikzjax.com/v1/fonts.css">
<script src="https://tikzjax.com/v1/tikzjax.js"></script>
Then in the
<body>
, include TikZ code such as
<script type="text/tikz">
\begin{tikzpicture}
\draw (0,0) circle (1in);
\end{tikzpicture}
</script>
Your TikZ will be compiled into SVGs; the
<script>
element will be
replaced with the corresponding SVG.  For instance, the above code generates
You can also use this for commutative diagrams.  For example, this code
<script type="text/tikz">
\begin{tikzcd}
A \arrow[r, "\phi"] \arrow[d, red]
& B \arrow[d, "\psi" red] \\
C \arrow[r, red, "\eta" blue]
& |[blue, rotate=-15]| D
\end{tikzcd}
</script>
will be rendered as
How does this work?
Using
web2js
, the Pascal source of
tex
is compiled to WebAssembly; the latex format is loaded (without all the hyphenation data), and
\documentclass[margin=0pt]{standalone}
\def\pgfsysdriver{pgfsys-ximera.def}
\usepackage{tikz}
is executed.  Then core is dumped; the resulting core is compressed, and by reloading the dumped core in the browser, it is possible to very quickly get to a point where TikZ can be executed.  By using an SVG driver for PGF along with
dvi2html
, the DVI output is converted to an SVG.
To emphasize this:
all of this happens in the browser.

data.title: Demystifying decorators: They don't need to be cryptic
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
本文由Stephen Gruppetta撰写，旨在阐明Python中的装饰器其实并不神秘。装饰器用于为函数添加可重用的功能，而不必定义新函数。作者通过七个部分逐步解释装饰器的工作原理，本文涵盖了第一和第二部分。

首先，作者介绍了闭包（Closures）的概念。通过一个例子，作者展示了如何在不修改全局变量的情况下记录所有传递给`print()`函数的参数。初始方案中，数据列表是局部变量，每次函数调用都会创建新列表，无法实现预期效果。接着，作者将数据列表设为全局变量，虽然解决了问题，但带来了其他代码可能意外修改该列表的风险。

理想的解决方案是使用闭包，将数据列表与函数局部作用域一起封装，使函数可以访问该数据，而其他代码不能。这通过定义一个包含所需数据和函数的外部函数实现，从而创建一个闭包。

作者承诺在后续文章中继续讲解装饰器的其他部分。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python装饰器及其相关概念（如闭包）的理解与实现方式

不同观点：
• notepad0x90认为直接调用双下划线函数（如`__closure__`）不是Pythonic的做法，建议通过实现类来覆盖或实现这些函数，并对文章中直接调用`__closure__`的方式是否适合生产代码提出质疑。
• admarples批评文章标题为“解析装饰器”却没有真正描述装饰器，认为文章未清晰解释装饰器的核心概念，并认为装饰器的核心只是一种特殊的函数调用语法，可以通过简单例子说明。
• sltkr对文章的受众和内容重点提出质疑，认为文章花了过多篇幅在闭包上，而闭包并非装饰器的核心，且`__closure__`属性只是实现细节。sltkr进一步解释装饰器的基本原理，并给出不使用闭包的装饰器实现例子，强调Python函数作为一等对象的核心概念。

补充讨论：
• notepad0x90提供了对`__closure__`用法的具体疑问，并提到文章可能为了说明主题而采用这种写法，但对其在生产代码中的适用性存疑。
• admarples期望文章能用简单明了的例子来解释装饰器的语法和作用，认为文章未能有效传达这一知识。
• sltkr详细解释了装饰器的多种实现方式，包括使用和不使用闭包的情况，强调装饰器本质上是高阶函数，通过函数的引用、调用和返回等特性实现功能扩展。

争议焦点：
• 文章是否有效地解释了装饰器的核心概念。
• 直接调用双下划线函数如`__closure__`是否合适，特别是在生产代码中的适用性。
• 闭包是否是理解和实现装饰器的必要条件。

"What on Earth is going on with decorators?" Is this you? They're not as hard as you think. But we need to get there step by step
Stephen Gruppetta

I avoided decorators for so long. First, I pretended they didn't exist. Then, I treated them like a magic spell—I'd use some of the common ones and simply copy how they're used in the documentation. And each time I tried to learn how they work, I'd give up pretty quickly.
But eventually, I got there. And once I finally understood how decorators work, my reaction was, "Is that it?" As with many complex topics, the magic goes away once you get it, and what's left makes perfect sense.
So, let me take you on a journey similar to the one I took to demystify decorators.
I split this decorator quest into seven parts. This article covers Parts 1 and 2. These are the most important parts to understand decorators. Take your time. I'll publish Parts 3 to 7 in a separate article soon.
Decorators are powerful for adding reusable functionality to functions without the need to define a new function. You’ll see them often in Python, and you may even need to write your own one at some point.
Part 1 • Closures
Part 1 introduces one of the main characters in this story—closures. We'll get to decorators in Part 2 later in this article.
Let's say you want to keep track of all the arguments you pass to all the calls to
print()
throughout your code. And no, you don't want to have to do this manually. You want your code to automatically keep a record of any argument you use when you call
print()
.
Start by defining a new function to replace the built-in
print()
. Although you could name this new function
print
, I'll add a trailing underscore in this example to keep the code focused on what really matters. First, here's a version that won't work as intended—the code runs without errors but doesn't achieve the result you need:
All code blocks are available in text format at the end of this article • #1 •
The code images used in this article are created using
Snappify
. [Affiliate link]
The new
print_()
function calls the built-in
print()
, but it also appends the argument to a list named
data
. Look for the trailing underscore in this article whenever I write
print_
or
print
!
However,
data
is defined within the function definition. Therefore,
data
is a
local variable
. It exists only when you call the function and while the program executes it. It cannot be accessed from anywhere else in the program. This variable is local to each function
call
.
The code creates a new list each time you call the function. That won't work. You need a single list that contains all the arguments you pass to all the
print_()
function calls.
A second option is to define the list
data
outside the function definition:
#2
The list
data
now exists in the
global scope
. And a function can access names defined in the global scope. Therefore, this solution works. Here's the output from this code:
I love Python
...and also The Python Coding Stack
['I love Python', '...and also The Python Coding Stack']
The list
data
now holds a record of all the arguments you pass to
print_()
.
This works. However, there are some drawbacks to this solution. The list
data
exists in the global scope and, therefore, can be accessed from anywhere in the code. There's the danger that another part of your code tries to access and modify this list, leading to bugs and unexpected behaviour:
#3
The list
data
now includes an object that's not been used as an argument in
print_()
:
['I love Python', '...and also The Python Coding Stack', 'Oops, modified globally!']
You want to eliminate this risk.
Also, you can only use this list with one function, the function
print_()
. If you want to keep track of arguments passed to other functions, you'll need to create a separate list with a separate name for each function.
In the first (wrong) solution above,
data
was local to the function. In this solution,
data
is global. Ideally, we need something in between these two options.
Creating a closure
Let me show the current version of the code again, but I'll visually highlight the function's scope:
#4
The ideal solution for this problem—the
in-between
solution in which
data
is neither local nor global—encloses the list
data
along with the function's local scope. Here's a visual representation of what
we'd like to achieve
:
#5
If we could create such a bubble or enclosure that includes the function's local scope and
data
, the function would still have access to
data
even though it's not a local variable. But the rest of the code won't be able to access and modify
data
.

理想的解决方案是使用闭包，将数据列表与函数局部作用域一起封装，使函数可以访问该数据，而其他代码不能。这通过定义一个包含所需数据和函数的外部函数实现，从而创建一个闭包。

作者承诺在后续文章中继续讲解装饰器的其他部分。

data.title: Better Error Handling
data.author: zdgeier
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了错误处理不当所带来的严重后果，如经济损失、空难、人员伤亡等，强调了错误处理在软件安全和可靠性方面的重要性。特别是在TypeScript和JavaScript中，传统的try/catch错误处理方法在简单场景下有效，但在复杂应用中面临挑战，如无法对错误进行类型检查、难以处理限流错误和聚合多个API调用错误等。文章还提到JavaScript允许抛出任何类型的错误，导致类型安全问题。最后，文章指出良好的堆栈跟踪能在一定程度上缓解错误跟踪问题，但传统方法仍存在局限性，需寻找更优的错误处理方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：错误处理的最佳实践和不同编程语言中的错误处理机制

不同观点：
• jackjeff：认为在每行代码后检查错误（如Go语言）是一种糟糕的做法，容易导致开发者忽视错误检查，从而产生难以调试的问题。相比之下，异常机制更为直观，虽然Monad等模式有其优势，但在JavaScript中使用会带来不必要的复杂性。同时，对重试机制持谨慎态度，认为重试可能引发其他问题。
• geocar：反驳认为即使在Rust等静态类型语言中也无法检查和处理所有错误，例如磁盘满错误是无法预见的。主张在多任务环境下通过用户干预解决此类问题，而不是完全依赖代码处理。
• zeroq：通过实际经验说明在已有代码库中引入错误处理和日志记录可能导致代码复杂化，即使从整洁的实现开始，最终也可能变得混乱。
• ivanjermakov：认为将错误作为值处理的方法有其局限性，尤其在函数签名需要更改时，会导致调用链上的每个调用者都需要更新。适合在程序需求明确且正确性优先于原型速度的情况下使用。
• medhir：质疑为何不直接使用.then().catch()处理异步调用中的错误，认为这比引入新模式更符合Go语言的做法。
• RadiozRadioz：指出JavaScript的错误处理本身较差，认为原生支持的类型检查和检查异常能解决许多问题。
• whatsakandr：希望C++默认是`nothrow`，并通过经验说明对不太可能失败的操作使用异常，对更可能失败的操作使用optional。
• kikimora：介绍Common Lisp中的重试机制，并希望现代语言也能引入类似功能。
• pmontra：介绍Erlang/Elixir的错误处理方法，包括返回包含ok或fail值的元组和模式匹配，并指出这些方法在其他语言中可能不适用。
• Animats：强调错误需要有用的分类，以便在捕获错误后知道如何处理，并批评Rust在这方面不够完善。
• eximius：希望语言在错误处理上更加标准化，包括堆栈跟踪、错误包装和多错误组合。
• Lord_Zero：指出“结果模式”在C#中早已存在，并非新概念。
• ChrisMarshallNY：认为最好的错误处理是尽量避免错误发生，通过良好的用户体验设计减少错误率，并在错误发生时以简明和同理的方式报告。
• havkom：主张在合适的代码层次处理特定类型的错误，避免在不合适的层次处理错误以减少代码复杂性和数据不一致问题。

补充讨论：
• 对重试机制的争议：jackjeff和pmontra对重试机制持谨慎态度，认为可能导致其他问题，而kikimora则希望引入类似Common Lisp的重试机制。
• 对JavaScript错误处理的普遍批评：多位评论者（如RadiozRadioz和jackjeff）指出JavaScript在错误处理方面的不足。
• 对错误分类和处理方法的讨论：Animats和geocar强调了错误分类和处理策略的重要性，并提供了实际例子。

通过这些观点，可以看到不同语言和开发者在错误处理上的偏好和实践各有不同，主要争议点在于是否应在每行代码后检查错误、如何有效地处理和分类错误以及如何在语言层面支持这些机制。

Bad error handling has cost billions of dollars, crashed planes, killed people, tanked stock markets, wrecked vehicles, and delayed flights. As we reflect on Halloween, it’s fitting to consider these horror stories of software gone wrong. You can read more about them in my
A Halloween scary story
, based on true events, or watch this newly minted Fireship video.
Thank God I didn’t fly during the CrowStrike incident (see what I did there?).
Error handling isn’t just a technical challenge - it’s a critical aspect of software safety and reliability. Yet in TypeScript and JavaScript, it remains something of a wild west. Today, I’ll share an overview of the current landscape and my preferred approaches.
The Current State of Error Handling

data.title: The appeal of serving your web pages with a single process
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问作者博客或wiki时会遇到浏览器被阻止的问题。原因在于，作者的反爬虫措施会屏蔽使用过旧版本的浏览器，尤其是某些旧版Chrome浏览器，这些版本常被高流量的数据爬虫用于训练大型语言模型。如果用户确实在使用当前浏览器版本却仍被阻止，可以联系作者提供所用浏览器的详细信息。此外，使用archive.*（如archive.today等）的用户也会被误拦，因为这些网站的爬虫行为与恶意爬虫相似，作者建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕系统架构设计中的扩展性、复杂性及性能的讨论

不同观点：
• kevmo314认为，过早考虑扩展性会导致不必要的复杂性和高成本。他描述了一个简单的服务因为过度设计，最终演变成一个昂贵且复杂的系统。这种做法不仅增加了基础设施的复杂性，还导致了组织内的僵化，因为相关人员不愿移除这些基础设施。
• torginus支持从单体架构开始，通过依赖注入在同一进程中运行所有服务，只有在需要时才进行横向和纵向扩展。他强调了这种方法在版本控制和部署上的简便性，并通过实际经验说明了如何在生产环境中成功应用。
• Lord_Zero指出，使用如ASPNET Core这样的框架，可以通过简单的配置实现限流，而不必担心线程或状态等问题，暗示了现代框架已经解决了部分扩展性问题。
• emacsen通过继承Node应用的经验，强调了单体应用在调试和运行时的便利性，但也指出了在升级和状态共享上的挑战，特别是在需要无缝升级或状态共享的情况下，复杂性不可避免地增加。
• remram建议在需要时可以实现进程内和Redis的限流方案，并通过接口进行切换，强调了在垂直扩展到必须水平扩展时的网络同步成本。
• stana对Python的单进程服务性能表示担忧，特别是由于GIL（全局解释器锁）的存在，可能导致性能问题。
• loxs分享了使用Rust和Axum构建单二进制文件的经验，并通过Cloudflare和Sqlite等工具实现了一个高效的个人项目架构。
• theideaofcoffee以讽刺的口吻建议直接使用静态页面，避免所有动态内容的复杂性，质疑了过度复杂的设计是否必要。

补充讨论：
• 关于单体架构与微服务架构的权衡：torginus和emacsen都提到了从单体架构开始，并在需要时进行扩展的经验，而kevmo314和emacsen则指出了过度设计和复杂性的问题。
• 性能与扩展性的技术选择：stana对Python的GIL提出了担忧，而loxs则展示了Rust在高性能单二进制文件构建中的应用。
• 对博客文章和链接的批评：theideaofcoffee对博客文章的数量和内容提出了质疑，认为部分技术讨论可能并不实用。

争议的焦点：
• 是否过早考虑扩展性：kevmo314和torginus强调了过早考虑扩展性带来的问题，而Lord_Zero和remram则指出现代工具和框架已经能够简化部分扩展性问题。

You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17
43725516.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问作者博客或wiki时会遇到浏览器被阻止的问题。原因在于，作者的反爬虫措施会屏蔽使用过旧版本的浏览器，尤其是某些旧版Chrome浏览器，这些版本常被高流量的数据爬虫用于训练大型语言模型。如果用户确实在使用当前浏览器版本却仍被阻止，可以联系作者提供所用浏览器的详细信息。此外，使用archive.*（如archive.today等）的用户也会被误拦，因为这些网站的爬虫行为与恶意爬虫相似，作者建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。

data.title: How encryption for Cinema Movies works
data.author: perryflynn
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了DCI（数字电影先导）电影分发和加密的工作原理。DCI标准定义了从文件格式、加密到放映系统的各个方面，确保电影的安全分发。DCP（数字电影包）包含电影的所有组件，KDM（密钥分发消息）则包含解密影片的加密信息。分发过程中，制片方生成DCP和DKDM（分发KDM），通过AES密钥加密，分发方再将DKDM和证书发送给影院，以验证和放映电影。投影系统包括服务器、媒体块和音频处理器，媒体块负责DRM和解密，确保影片实时解密和播放。DCP格式为包含XML元数据和MXF视频文件的文件夹，命名有特定模式以标识电影的不同属性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字影院技术，尤其是DCP（Digital Cinema Package）的加密、文件格式、色彩处理以及相关的技术挑战和商业模式问题。

不同观点：
• **支持并推荐深入了解**：andreashaerter 推荐了一位作者在Chaos Computer Club活动中关于数字影院后台的演讲，介绍了数字放映系统、端到端加密、以及如何防止盗版的细节。这提供了对影院技术更深层次的理解。
  
• **技术细节澄清**：asdcplib 作为相关技术库的作者，澄清了DCP的颜色空间、加密方式（逐帧加密而不是整个流加密），以及FPGA在解密、解码、色彩处理中的作用。他还强调DCP是B2B格式，通过合同而非EULA授权，与一般的DRM有所不同。

• **时间线疑惑**：hbcondo714 对文章提到的时间线感到困惑，因为文章链接的讨论是在“昨天”创建的，但规格更新是在2024年，文章本身是去年写的。

• **加密安全性质疑**：dherls 和 jackjeff 对逐帧使用相同AES密钥加密的做法提出质疑，认为这类似于ECB模式，存在安全隐患。jackjeff 建议使用像XTS这样的方法来为每个帧生成独特的密钥。

• **盗版问题讨论**：john01dav 指出，尽管有复杂的加密和DRM保护，盗版电影仍然很容易找到，质疑影院在设备控制权上的牺牲是否值得。

• **水印和反盗版措施的争议**：NoMoreNicksLeft 提到DCP中的水印包含放映系统的序列号，若电影被盗录，影院将面临严重问题。但他也质疑，是否可以通过从不同放映机中导出电影并模糊水印来绕过这一措施。

• **历史技术挑战**：KaiserPro 回顾了2011年时DCP打包的复杂性和硬件需求，指出当时JPEG2000编码需要专门硬件才能接近实时性能。

• **对DRM和标准的批评**：shmerl 批评DRM本质上是为了从参与者身上获取更多利益，尤其是需要购买的标准，暗示整个系统是剥削性的。

• **行业趋势观察**：jeffbee 指出，在2024年美国票房收入下降的背景下，整个影院行业可能正在走向终结。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现的复杂性与历史演变：从早期的硬件需求到现代的解码和处理技术，评论中多次提到技术实现的难度以及随时间的变化。
• 加密安全性与盗版防范的争议焦点：对加密方式的安全性以及水印技术的有效性存在较多质疑和讨论，尤其是对逐帧加密和静态密钥使用的担忧。
• 行业发展趋势：有评论提到了影院行业面临的票房收入下降问题，暗示了技术发展背后更大的商业和行业背景。

43745281.article_content:
How DCI Movie Delivery and Encryption works
31. May 2024
Â·
christian Â·
digital cinema
,
projects
,
reverse engineering
,
security
The Cinema Industry is using its own standards for creating and distributing movies in a secure way. The DCI (Digital Cinema Initiatives) specification defines everything from file formats and encryption to the projection systems itself.
The specification itself is
publicly available
but relies on various IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers) and SMPTE (Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers) standards, which have to be purchased.
Scope
This document will show a rough overview of the DCI workflow and describe in detail how the encryption of a DCI movie works. It will
not
show how to break any encryption and no encryption has been broken while writing this document.
From our perspective, the DCI standard is safe
.
The author of this document has been operating a cinema since 2021, without any insight to the distribution or production side of the industry. Some information may be incomplete.
How itâs started
End of 2023 the movie
WONKA
was released. Some cinemas reported, that they are unable to start this movie on their projector.
The reason was, that a certificate used by the distributor was expired. This certificate was used to sign the DCP files.
The distributor published new files, starting the movie worked again.
Out of curiosity the author started to check how the validation process on the projector is working.
Glossar
DCP
: Digital Cinema Package - A folder which contains all components of a movie. Metadata, Subtitles, Audio and Picture in seperate files
CPL
: Composition Playlist - A DCP can contain multiple audio and video streams which will combined in a CPL
KDM
: Key Delivery Message - A XML file which contains the cryptographical information to allow a movie playback on a specific DCI certified projection system
DKDM
: Distribution Key Delivery Message - Similar to a KDM, but for a remastering or distribution system, not for a projection system
Distribution Process
graph TD
classDef red fill:#a91900
classDef green fill:#126500
classDef purple fill:#650072
legendprod[Producer]:::red
legenddist[Distributor]:::green
legendcine[Cinema]:::purple
legendvendors[Projector Manufacturer]
graph LR
classDef red fill:#a91900
classDef green fill:#126500
classDef purple fill:#650072
dcpcreated(["DCP\ncreated"]):::red --"AES Key"--> dkdmcreated
dkdmcreated(["DKDM\ncreated"]):::red --"encrypted\nAES Key"--> dkdmp
dkdmp[DKDM]:::green --> verify(["Projector\nverified"]):::green
dcpcreated --"to Distributor"--> dcp(["DCP by\nDownload or\nHarddrive"]):::green
distcert["Distributor\nCertificate"]:::green --"to Producer"--> dkdmcreated
verify --"to Cinema"--> kdm[KDM]:::purple
dcp --"to Cinema"--> dcp2["DCP"]:::purple
cinecert["Projector\nCertificate"]:::purple --"to Distributor"--> verify
trusted["Trusted Device List"] --> verify
dcp2 --> projector[Projector]:::purple
kdm --> projector
Projection Systems
Most of the Projection Systems consists of Server, Audio Processor and Projector.
graph LR
server[Server] --> mediablock[Media Block]
hdmi[HDMI Source] --> splitter[Audio Splitter]
splitter --"Video"--> projector
splitter --"Audio"--> sound
subgraph Projector
mediablock --"Video"--> projector[Projector]
end
projector --> screen[Theatre Screen]
mediablock --"Audio"--> sound[Audio Processor]
sound --> speakers[Speakers]
The Server stores the DCPs and KDMs, manages Playlists and controls the Projector and Audio Processor hardware.
Many Cinemas also connect their Theatre Automation (light, curtains, etc.) to the projector. By setting time-based commands into the playlists, lights and screen curtain can be controlled automatically. The Projector Server provides 12V/24V relays for this.
These time-based commands are also used to set the correct Aspect Ratio and Volume on the different DCPs in a Playlist.
The Server can be controlled remotely by a PC or in larger cinemas by a Theatre Management System.
The DCPs are imported from USB/CRU hard drives or by internet download to the server. They are stored encrypted at all times.
The projector includes a so called âMedia Blockâ which handles DRM and decryption. It receives the DCP data and the KDM to decrypt each frame in real time.
On DCP playback the Projector will send the decrypted PCM audio to the Audio Processor which will then send each processed Audio Channel to the respective Speakers.
DCP Format
A DCP is a folder which contains XML metadata files and multiple MXF files for the actual movie.
Folder Naming Pattern
AwesomeMovie_FTR-2_S_DE-XX_DE-16_51_4K_20240119_SMPTE_OV
AwesomeMovie
: A short version of the movie title
FTR
: Media Type, in this case âFeatureâ
2
: Version Number
S
: Aspect ratio, in this case 2.35:1 aka âSopeâ
DE
: Audio Language
XX
: Subtitle Language, in this case is no subtitle available
DE
: Territory
16
: Age Rating
51
: Audio channels, in this case 5.1 surround sound
4K
: Mov

43747242.article_content:
Abstract
A sustained, coordinated social media harassment and doxxing campaign – which we codenamed JUICYJAM – targeting the pro-democracy movement in Thailand has run uninterrupted, and unchallenged, since at least August 2020. We define doxxing as the search for and the publication of an individual’s personal data on the Internet with malicious intent, in this instance, to suppress and harass the Thai pro-democracy movement. The operation utilized an inauthentic persona over multiple social media platforms (primarily X and Facebook) to target pro-democracy protesters by doxxing individuals, continuously harassing them, and instructing followers to report them to the police. Through our analysis of public social media posts we determined that the campaign was not only inauthentic, but the information revealed could not have been reasonably sourced from a private individual. Thanks to a public leak of confidential military and police documents in March 2025, we can now attribute the campaign to the Royal Thai Armed Forces and/or the Royal Thai Police. With a high rate of following and engagement across platforms, JUICYJAM is an uncommon instance of a successful state-sponsored influence operation. JUICYJAM’s tactics support a larger network of judicial harassment and democratic suppression that is infrequently enforced by social media platforms, but poses a significant threat to civil society.
Key Findings
Since at least August 2020, a coordinated social media harassment and doxxing campaign targeting the Thai pro-democracy movement has run uninterrupted and unchallenged. We codenamed it JUICYJAM.
Thanks to a public leak of confidential military and police documents that occurred in March 2025, we can now attribute the campaign to the Royal Thai Armed Forces and/or the Royal Thai Police, whose online repression efforts have allegedly been merged into a joint “Cyber Team” since 2023.
The campaign operates within a broader context of dissent repression tactics, both online and offline, that closely resemble those we have previously analyzed in other regions – such as, for example, in Hong Kong.
JUICYJAM’s longstanding, uninterrupted activity over multiple social media platforms (primarily X and Facebook) once again exposes the shortcomings of platforms in creating and enforcing policies on highly coordinated and harmful doxxing campaigns intended to suppress civil society.
Platforms’ policies on doxxing seldom consider the behaviour in the context of coordinated – and often state-sponsored – campaigns against civil society. They also do not consider environmental factors, such as the doxxing happening during unrest and protests.
Background
In 2014, Thailand faced its second military coup of the century, placing a military junta – the National Council for Peace and Order – in power. The junta immediately imposed martial law, ratified a military-backed constitution, and, in 2019, the former army chief who led the coup, Prayuth Chan-o-cha, was elected Prime Minister. In July 2020, youth-led pro-democracy protests broke out across the country, demanding a more democratic constitution and reforms to the monarchy. The protesters were met with severe repression, and after a two-year
pause
of prosecutions, in November 2020, Prime Minister Prayuth ordered authorities to bring back the enforcement of
lèse-majesté
, or Section 112 of the Criminal Code, which criminalizes “insulting the monarchy”. Thailand’s use of
lèse-majesté
has been both arbitrary and prolific; protesters can be arrested for as little as
sharing social media posts
that are ‘insulting to the monarchy’. Furthermore, the weaponization of
lèse-majesté
has devastating consequences: those convicted under Section 112 face three to 15 years in prison per count. Thai authorities have extensively used
lèse-majesté
as a tool to punish pro-democracy advocates, with around 270 protesters detained and convicted
since 2020
.
Weaponizing the judiciary has not been enough, however. Since the 2014 coup, the Thai pro-democracy movement has been heavily targeted through various digital means. In 2022, Citizen Lab researchers uncovered an extensive
espionage campaign
impacting several groups within the movement, such as FreeYOUTH and WeVo. In fact, one of the authors of this report, Katekanok Wongsapakdee, was also found to be targeted.
Additionally,
multiple influence operations
(IOs) have been exposed for their attempts to discredit the pro-democracy movement and intimidate its members. In October 2020, the company now called X (formerly Twitter) exposed one of the most notorious online IOs targeting the Thai protest movement when it
announced
the removal of 926 covertly coordinated accounts. The network of accounts was attributed with high confidence to the Royal Thai Army (RTA). Twitter found the accounts to be “engaging in amplifying pro-RTA and pro-government content, as well as engaging in behavior targeting prominent political opposition figures.”

data.title: X-Ray Defence
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 本文是关于国际象棋中的X光防御（X-ray Defence）技巧，作为系列的第二部分，重点探讨如何利用X光防御拯救看似无解的局面。X光防御指的是一个棋子通过另一个棋子间接保护某个关键格子或棋子。文章通过多个实例展示了如何在防守中运用X光技巧，例如在无法直接防守时，通过X光防御间接保护重要棋子或避免被将杀。这些例子逐步增加难度，展示了防守方如何在看似必败的局面中找到隐藏的生机。文章强调，防守技巧在棋艺发展中同样重要，发现这些防守资源可以挽救许多对局。通过这些例子，作者希望展示防守战术与进攻战术一样有趣且关键。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[国际象棋中的防守策略，尤其是X射线防守（X-ray defense）的有效性及训练不足的问题]

不同观点：
• [kazinator的观点]  
  - X射线防守的有效性依赖于特定棋子位置的保护。例如，白方车之所以能防守住，是因为有白方皇后从上方保护它。如果没有皇后的保护，黑方皇后可以直接吃掉白车。  
  - 支持当前棋盘配置中防守线能够穿透敌方棋子的观点，认为这些防守被称为“X射线”是因为它们预见了未来可能的棋局变化（如某个敌方棋子移开后，攻击路线依然有效）。

• [captn3m0的观点]  
  - 认为防守战术和相关的谜题在国际象棋文献和资源中被低估和忽视。  
  - 以Lichess上的Storm模式为例，指出自己虽然擅长发现好的进攻机会，但在防守方面训练不足，导致难以识别好的防守策略。

补充讨论：
• [训练不平衡的问题]  
  - captn3m0提到，很多棋手在训练中更注重进攻而忽视防守，这导致了对防守技巧的掌握不足。  
  - 这种训练不平衡可能导致棋手在实际对局中难以应对复杂的防守局面。

争议焦点：
• [X射线防守的具体条件]  
  - kazinator强调X射线防守的有效性依赖于特定棋子位置的保护，而不仅仅是防守线的穿透能力。这引出了一个问题：在何种条件下，X射线防守才能真正发挥作用？

• [防守训练的不足]  
  - captn3m0指出防守训练资源的不足，这表明在国际象棋教育和资源分配上可能存在偏重进攻、忽视防守的倾向。

总结：讨论主要围绕X射线防守的有效性和防守战术训练不足的问题展开。kazinator具体分析了X射线防守的棋局条件，而captn3m0则从更广泛的训练和资源角度提出了防守被忽视的观点。两者共同指向了防守在国际象棋中的重要性和当前存在的挑战。

43721853.article_content:
X-Ray Defence: Hidden Resource, Sudden Lifeline
Mcie
Apr 17, 2025
72
3,682
views
English (US)
Chess
Analysis
Puzzle
Tactics
Strategy
X-rays that save your position from surprising angles
Todays article is part 2 of 2 in my mini-lesson series on the X-ray motif. This follows up on my previous article which you can find in my blog here on Lichess or in the link for the original article:
X-Ray Attacks: Hidden Pressure, Sudden Impact
. If you haven’t seen that one yet be sure to check it out, as it introduces the theme and covers attacking patterns and puzzles involving the X-ray motif.
While in the first article we explored the offensive potential of the X-ray, in this lesson we flip the board and explore
X-rays as a defensive motif
. This is far less charted but equally important to grasp. As we defined in the previous lesson,
X-rays involve a piece eyeing a square
through
the body of another piece.
Even though the contact in indirect, the influence is still exerted within the line of sight of our piece. We’ve seen how is utilised in attacking themes, but this can work to your favour defensively too! This is demonstrated by the below example:
Defensive X-ray – Introductory Example:
We have to guard Black’s checkmate threat on g2. Rg1 is not available, but there is another defence:
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/rRKXjK1f#0
Rb2 indirectly defends g2 via an X-ray through Blacks Qf2. White’s will survive Blacks attack and will win by material.
In general, defensive tactics and puzzles are underrepresented in chess literature and resources. Probably because brilliant attacks are more satisfying to execute and solve, and defence generally does not attract attention. But learning to spot defensive resources is just as important to our chess development. Every player will be attacked and learning how to survive will save many points.
In the following six examples of gradual difficulty, we’ll explore how an X-ray defence holds the position together when the position looked gloom otherwise. Just like in the introductory example, in each case the defender seems to be in trouble, but a hidden lifeline lurks if you can identify the X-ray motif. Hopefully these examples show that defensive puzzles are just as interesting as attacking ones!
Position 1: Black to move
Black is up a pawn but hadn’t castled and looks to be in a deadly pin. Is it all over or can you find the resource to save the position?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/8uPj5Ztl#0
Yes!, defensive moves can be pleasing too! Ba4 is the only move to save black, and it is via an X-ray defence of Nc6 through Whites Bishop. The key is to see that Ba4 has indirect contact with Nc6 which becomes direct contact as soon as Whites Bishop takes, and therefore Ba4 does in fact defend Nc6.
Position 2: Black to play
Now Black seems to be in trouble on the back rank. Can Black save the Rook and thereby his King?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/bgNTDUOs#0
Black could not directly defend his rook but an X-ray defence by Qa8 through Whites Queen saves the day. Note the X-ray defence is mutual, as Re8 also defends Qa8 if White takes the Queen.
The move Qa8 is particularly difficult to spot as it is both X-ray and backwards move, both of which can be blind spots in our tactical visions. If you want more examples of these types of counterintuitive retreating moves, be sure to check out my previous lesson “
Don’t forget about backward moves!
“
Position 3: Black to play
White has sacrificed a piece and is threatening a menacing checkmate on h7. Can it be defended at all?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/XG7pnvnV#0
Again the only move that holds Blacks position is an X-ray, unconventionally defending h7 via Bd3 through Whites Queen. White’s attack is over and this again shows the importance of indirect line of sight. The next example combines defence and counterattack:
Position 4: White to play
Black has White in check thinking it forces a Queen trade leading to a winning endgame. Do you have a resource in the position?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/KYPFvZ0L#0
Hopefully the not-so-obvious yet powerful move was not so difficult to find. If this was the case, well done! This is pattern recognition kicking in and your tactical radar gained another weapon to use in your games!
For the final 2 examples I have ramped up the difficulty. There will be more moves to calculate but your tactical visions should be strong and you know what to look for.
Position 5: White to play
This was from my very own game playing White against a 2100+. Black has gone all in with the not-so-subtle plan of Qf3-g2, even leaving their Bd6 to be taken. Can we take it or are we falling into Blacks plan if we do? Or should we look to guard f3 instead?
https://lichess.org/study/kWe6Ipj6/swjFiKlb#0
Yet another incredible save, an X-ray defence of g2 via a8. This example shows that defensive ideas can even win us games if we spot them before our opponent, as it meant we could safely grab Blacks Bishop on d

Test Spies in Haskell
April 18
th
, 2025
| Sopot, Poland
Subscribe
When testing a web application, you often want to make sure that a certain
email
would
be sent — without actually sending it. How do you test that?
Take something like a transactional email: a user signs up, resets their
password, or completes a purchase — and your application needs to send a
notification. You don’t care how the email gets sent — just that it was
triggered correctly.
The simplest implementation for the email-sending function might look like this.

::

All this function needs to know is where to send the email. How it sends it
isn’t important here — and it’s not what we’re testing. What we care about is
how it’s called.
This function might be called from a request handler, and it would be that
handler function’s responsibility to decide how to call the email sending
function.

Handler
()

"user@example.com"

test spy
.
Spies are stubs that also record some information based on how they were called.
You can emulate a test spy using the same
stubbing method
I wrote about
earlier. Instead of calling
sendEmail
directly, you’ll retrieve it from

sendEmail

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在天气预报和相关报道中正确使用带重音字符（如ñ）的讨论

不同观点：
• [gumboshoes的观点] 认为美联社（Associated Press）早就应该在所有地方使用ñ，看到"La Nina"和"El Nino"而不是"La Niña"和"El Niño"让人感到尴尬。他认为在当前技术条件下，无法处理重音字符的系统是不可接受的，并质疑是否仍然存在仅支持ASCII字符的版本。

• [ece的观点] 表示希望在普通天气预报中提到这些细节，似乎更关注公众在常规信息获取中能接触到正确的术语和字符使用。

补充讨论：
- [gumboshoes] 提到对技术系统处理重音字符能力的质疑，暗示可能存在历史遗留的技术问题或不同版本的信息源。
- [ece] 的评论则更侧重于天气预报的普及性和教育性，希望这些细节能在日常媒体中得到体现。
- 争议的焦点似乎在于是否应在主流媒体和日常信息传播中普及正确的字符使用，尤其是在涉及外来术语和文化尊重的背景下。

data.title: "Upgrade" has become the most frightening word in the English language (2016)
data.author: lvnfg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对操作系统及软件升级带来的问题和影响的讨论

不同观点：
• [cookiengineer] 认为微软强制升级到云优先的操作系统，忽略了许多行业的实际需求，导致一些工厂和企业不得不切换到开源系统。他举例说，一家钢铁厂因升级导致生产中断，损失了数百万欧元，最终切换到开源系统并重新实现所有功能。他认为微软与实际需求脱节，且升级带来了不必要的风险和损失。

• [netsharc] 提到了手机应用自动更新带来的隐私问题。他举例说，更新后的Sony耳机应用包含了新的用户协议和选择性加入条款，可能涉及上传音乐和视频的标题和艺术家信息。他还提到更新后的耳机存在技术问题，比如不必要的自动关机和无法关闭的触控手势，这些问题让他感到困扰。

• [randycupertino] 讨论了家庭成员对手机和桌面操作系统更新的抵触情绪，尤其是当更新导致用户体验变差或功能被移除时。他提到自己的母亲需要帮助才能登录健康系统，反映了一些用户对操作系统更新适应困难的问题。

• [zx8080] 指出软件升级需要质量保证（QA）来确保升级的可行性，并提到有关微软仅依赖遥测数据而不进行适当QA的传言。他认为这种做法使得用户对升级持怀疑态度。

• [ronsor] 支持[cookiengineer]的观点，认为微软每次的Windows更新都让系统变得更差，这让人感到疲惫。

• [AStonesThrow] 通过一个购物体验的比喻，暗示商店重新配置（升级）可能是为了迷惑顾客，使他们花费更多时间寻找商品，从而增加不必要的消费。这反映了升级有时可能出于商业策略而非用户需求。

补充讨论：
• 微软的升级策略被多个评论者批评，认为其忽略了实际用户需求，带来了不便和风险。
• 应用和操作系统的自动更新可能涉及隐私问题，用户对新条款和功能的不满增加。
• 一些用户对更新后的技术问题感到困扰，特别是当这些问题影响日常使用时。
• 升级可能出于商业利益考虑，而非单纯为了提升用户体验。

data.title: Show HN: I built a tool that texts you if your server goes down
data.author: SantiagoVargas
data.article_summary: "YourServerIsDown" 是一个服务器监控服务，帮助企业避免因服务器宕机导致客户流失。用户注册后，可在30秒内开始监控服务器，并设置国际电话号码接收宕机短信提醒。服务覆盖全球多个国家和地区，用户需提供服务器健康端点URL，即可实时获取宕机通知，快速解决问题，防止销售损失和客户流失。注册即同意服务条款和隐私政策，已有账户可查看状态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服务器宕机监控工具的比较和使用场景

不同观点：
• SantiagoVargas：认为自己开发的YourServerIsDown.com作为一个辅助项目，能够满足其初创公司的基本需求，尤其是当服务器宕机时可以快速通知。他提到该工具简单、易于设置，并能避免每月支付Twilio/SMS费用。他还提供了一个AWS原生解决方案的替代方法，即通过Cloudwatch报警监控ALB的503错误，并发送通知到Slack或SNS。

• cocoa19：认为该工具不适合大多数企业服务，企业通常需要更全面的监控和告警系统，例如Thousand Eyes，并且通常不会将健康检查端点暴露给外部世界，因为这存在安全风险。

• bitbasher：对辅助项目表示赞赏，但指出此类通知系统常产生误报，导致额外的时间成本。他还质疑如果服务没有用户或用户不报告问题，是否真的存在宕机问题。他个人依赖客户的邮件反馈来发现服务问题。

• vivzkestrel：关注如何确定服务器宕机，但没有具体展开所使用的技术和方法。

补充讨论：
• SantiagoVargas提供了实际的解决方案，并分享了开发背景和动机，强调了简单易用的特点，适合不需要复杂功能的用户。
• cocoa19则从企业级需求的角度出发，强调了安全性及全面监控的必要性，认为该工具不适合企业级应用。
• bitbasher对工具的实际效果提出质疑，特别是误报问题，并分享了自己对服务监控的看法，即依赖用户反馈而非主动监控。
• vivzkestrel的问题引发了对宕机检测方法的思考，但未深入讨论具体技术细节。

争议焦点：该工具的适用场景和误报问题。SantiagoVargas强调其工具的简单实用，而cocoa19和bitbasher则对其适用性和实际效果提出质疑。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了对TikTok虚拟机（VM）的逆向工程项目，主要目标是解密和反混淆`webmssdk.js`文件。该文件使用了多种混淆技术，如通过数组索引进行变量访问和函数调用，导致代码难以阅读。项目提供了多种工具来反混淆代码、将虚拟机指令反编译为可读形式，并通过脚本注入替换混淆的VM。

文章详细描述了如何处理两种主要的混淆方法：
1. **变量名和函数名的混淆**：通过执行混淆数组代码，还原出原始字符串，再用正则表达式替换代码中的混淆用法。
2. **函数调用的混淆**：将数组中的函数定义替换为标准函数调用，使代码更易读。

项目还解决了虚拟机字节码的解密问题。字节码通过XOR加密存储，解密后可理解VM的工作原理。最终，通过自动化工具和AI的帮助，成功将代码还原为更易读的版本。

TikTok VM Reverse Engineering (webmssdk.js)
This project is for reverse engineering the TikTok Virtual Machine (VM).
Overview
TikTok uses a custom virtual machine (VM) as part of its obfuscation and security layers. This project includes tools to:
Deobfuscate
webmssdk.js
that has the virtual machine.
Decompile
TikTok’s virtual machine instructions into readable form.
Script Inject
Replace webmssdk.js with the deobfuscated VM
injector
.
Sign URLs

data.title: The Effect of Deactivating Facebook and Instagram on Users' Emotional State
data.author: imakwana
data.article_summary: 这篇文章研究了在2020年美国大选前，停用Facebook和Instagram对用户情绪状态的影响。通过两项大型随机实验发现，停用Facebook六周的用户在幸福感、抑郁和焦虑指数上改善了0.060个标准差，而停用Instagram的用户改善了0.041个标准差。进一步分析显示，Facebook的影响主要体现在35岁以上人群，而Instagram的影响主要来自25岁以下的女性。文章作者中有多人曾接受Meta（Facebook母公司）的资助或参与其活动，披露了潜在的利益冲突。

• 社交媒体的成瘾性和心理影响：[donatj] 和 [Kozmik1] 强调了社交媒体成瘾及其对心理健康的负面影响。[donatj] 描述了社交媒体互动减少后的孤独感，而[Kozmik1] 则观察到家庭成员因沉迷Facebook而忽略家庭互动。

• 对社交媒体脱离效果的质疑：[nomilk] 和 [perching_aix] 对研究结果表示怀疑，认为脱离社交媒体对幸福感的影响微乎其微，且效果因人而异。[rimeice] 进一步指出，六周的时间可能不足以观察到长期效果。

• 对特定平台的批评：[Arisaka1] 批评LinkedIn的“高光效应”，认为这种展示成功的文化对求职者的心理健康不利。

补充讨论：
• 社交媒体在社会活动中的不可或缺性：[kleiba] 和 [johnisgood] 提到即使不愿意使用社交媒体，但由于社会压力和家庭需求，完全脱离变得不现实。

• 替代社交媒体的方式：[8s2ngy] 希望有更小、更私密的社交网络，而[donatj] 则转向与AI进行对话以弥补社交互动的缺失。

• 长期效果的关注：[veunes] 提出对脱离社交媒体后重新激活账号是否会使改善效果消失的疑问。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体对心理健康和幸福感的实际影响程度存在不同看法，部分人认为影响微小，而其他人则感受到显著的负面影响。
• 完全脱离社交媒体的可行性和现实性，尤其是在社交活动日益依赖社交媒体的背景下。
