Shawn Fain: Workers Deserve More Time for Themselves
Shawn Fain
Why Bidenism Failed
Brent Cebul
Lily Geismer
Inflation Kills Governments
Isabella Weber
The Working Class Has Left the Building
Jared Abbott
In evolutionary biology, one of those mysterious thresholds of which at present we have only the vaguest conceptual grasp is that moment in the ramification of any phylogenic series at which an irrevocable taxonomic divergence occurs, and a genuinely new species emerges. Traces of the event linger on in the paleontological record and the sequences of the genome, of course, but only in a fragmentary way. Only at the end of the process can we say with some assurance that a cow is most definitely not a whale, and that neither (to its credit) is a corporate attorney. But, of course, we expect nature to be capricious, and since the time of Darwin especially we have learned to find it unsurprising that horses and snails should have arisen out of precursors that did not even dimly adumbrate what horses and snails would eventually be.
Our expectations of human history, however, tend to be somewhat more “essentialist” than that, principally because our institutions and orders of power constantly rewrite the past to establish their own pedigrees. Most of us are able to inhabit and find shelter in cultural, social, political, and religious structures precisely because we trust in their unity, stability, and constancy over time. And even those of us who are anything but Hegelians are likely to believe that there is some kind of rational consistency to history’s disclosure of human possibilities, and that we can explain how the Renaissance sprang from the late Middle Ages with something like the same precision with which we can explain the course of a river reaching the sea. The result of thinking that way, though, can be fairly fantastic, rather like working on the assumption that whales, cows, and corporate attorneys constitute a single species.
All of which is a very circuitous way of saying that there is not, and has never been, a single identifiable thing that we can call “Christianity” except with excruciating generality. From the very first, “the Way” (as it was originally known among its adherents) was like a kind of pluripotential genetic code waiting to be developed by epigenetic forces; and down the centuries, its expressions continuously evolved and diverged into countless unanticipated and ultimately incommiscible breeds. This is not to say that the original “genetic” impulse was random, incidentally; I happen to believe, for instance, that the first followers of Jesus of Nazareth truly did have real experiences of him as alive again after his crucifixion, and that that is why their movement did not dissolve upon his death (though this is not the place to argue the point). It is only to say that there are many religious phenomena out there — such as the great mainstream of American white Evangelicalism — to which we apply the word “Christianity” about as meaningfully as we might apply the word “dinosaur” to a sparrow (there have, you see, been a few developments since those days).
Most modern (and especially most American) Christians are quite accustomed, for instance, to thinking of Christianity as a fairly commonsensical creed as regards the practicalities of life. On the matter of wealth, they take it as given that, while the New Testament enjoins generosity to the poor, it otherwise allows the wealthy to enjoy the fruits of their industry or fair fortune with a clean conscience. Common sense tells them that it is not wealth as such that the New Testament condemns, but only a spiritually unhealthy preoccupation with it — the idolatry of riches, wealth misused, wealth immorally gained; riches in and of themselves, surely, are neither good nor bad. But in fact, one thing in startlingly short supply in the New Testament is common sense, and the commonsensical view of the early church is invariably the wrong one. In point of fact, the New Testament, alarmingly enough, condemns personal wealth not merely as a moral danger, but as an
intrinsic
evil. Actually, the texts are so unambiguous on this matter that it requires an almost heroic defiance of the obvious to fail to grasp their import. Admittedly, many translations down the centuries have had an emollient effect on a few of the New Testament’s severer pronouncements. But this is an old story.
Jesus condemned not only an unhealthy preoccupation with riches, but the getting and keeping of riches as such.
Take, for example, the word used in Christian scripture for one of the principal virtues of the new movement: κοινωνία, or
koinōnia

43745088.article_summary: 《Progress》期刊春季版发布，现可订阅印刷版。本期包含多篇文章：Shawn Fain讨论工人应获得更多个人时间；Brent Cebul和Lily Geismer分析拜登政策的失败；Isabella Weber探讨通货膨胀对政府的影响；Jared Abbott则聚焦工人阶级的变化。此外，文章还通过进化生物学类比，指出人类历史和制度常被赋予过于“本质化”的期望，而基督教自起源以来也经历了诸多演变，不同教派有着显著差异。特别是，新约实际上将个人财富视为内在的恶，而非仅是痴迷于财富的问题。这些文章挑战了人们对历史和宗教的常见假设。

data.title: First hormone-free male birth control pill enters human trials
data.author: Teever
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型男性避孕药YCT-529的安全性、有效性及相关机制的讨论

不同观点：
• **对药物长期安全性的担忧**：[thecupisblue] 和 [w10-1] 对YCT-529长期使用的安全性提出质疑。[thecupisblue] 担心长期抑制RARα受体会导致其他RAR受体（如RARβ和γ）代偿，可能引发副作用，尤其是RARα在细胞发育和凋亡中的作用与某些癌症有关。[w10-1] 进一步指出，RARα途径在血细胞发育和凋亡中起到重要作用，长期使用可能会带来不确定的风险，甚至影响后代。

• **与其他非激素男性避孕方法的比较**：[johnisgood] 提到现有的非激素男性避孕药，如α-受体阻滞剂（例如Silodosin），也能达到90-99%的避孕效果，且不会影响性欲，停药后立即可逆。他暗示这种方法可能比YCT-529更成熟，建议大家尝试和比较。

• **热力避孕法**：[Voultapher] 提出目前已有基于热力的非激素男性避孕方法，尽管不广为人知，但有科学支持。他提到1930年代在印度进行的长期研究显示该方法没有长期副作用，并表示可以提供更多研究链接。

• **对99%有效性的质疑**：[hwpythonner] 和 [pftburger] 对YCT-529的99%有效性提出实际使用中的质疑。[hwpythonner] 询问是否包含不按时服药的情况，而[pftburger] 则指出99%的有效性意味着每年仍可能有三个意外怀孕的案例。

• **对药物其他功能的幽默或讽刺评论**：[khazhoux] 开玩笑地提到，发明一种消除男性不应期的药物将带来巨大财富，而[panny] 则讽刺地表示担心这种药物会被添加到公共水 supply 中。[anonym29] 则用讽刺的语气表示，这种避孕方法是否会像其他流行文化现象一样被追捧。

补充讨论：
• **对讨论质量的关注**：[thecupisblue] 在一开始提到，这个话题下的许多评论更像是为了获取点赞（"karma farming"），而不是为了深入讨论，呼吁大家更认真地参与讨论。

• **对科学进展的积极评价**：[Ericson2314] 对YCT-529的研发表示惊喜和乐观，认为这是科学资助的成果，并希望这能促使更多人对科学研究进行反思和支持。

争议焦点：YCT-529的长期安全性及其与其他非激素避孕方法的比较是讨论中的主要争议点。部分评论者对其有效性和实际应用中的可行性提出质疑，而另一些评论者则关注其潜在的副作用和风险。

data.author: Venn1
data.article_summary: PiLiDAR是一个DIY项目，旨在创建一个360°的3D全景扫描仪。该项目使用LDRobot的LiDAR传感器（如LD06、LD19或STL27L）进行扫描，结合Raspberry Pi和HQ Camera进行全景照片拍摄。系统通过自定义串行驱动程序和CRC校验确保数据完整性，并支持2D实时可视化和导出。全景图使用Hugin软件拼接，3D场景通过Open3D进行可视化和导出，支持多种格式。硬件方面，项目使用Raspberry Pi 4、NEMA17步进电机和A4988驱动器，供电可选择18650电池或USB电源银行。项目还涉及GPIO中断处理、I2C配置和UART设置等技术细节，以实现完整的扫描和数据处理流程。

[Unit]

After=network.target

Type=simple

ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /home/pi/PiLiDAR/gpio_interrupt.py

WantedBy=multi-user.target
reload daemon, enable and start service:

sudo systemctl start pilidar.service
check service if necessary:
sudo systemctl status pilidar.service
set Permission for UART on Raspberry Pi
temporary solution:
sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
old solution: make it permanent by disabling password for chmod:
sudo visudo
pi ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
then execute the
temporary
solution from python:
import subprocess
command = "sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0"

data.title: Let's give PRO/VENIX a barely adequate, pre-C89 TCP/IP stack, featuring Slirp-CK
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者多年前计划为Commodore 64编写TCP/IP协议栈，但未付诸实践。与此同时，其他人成功实现了这一目标。作者曾购买TCP/IP Illustrated书籍，但一直未拆封。如今，借助AI和更多现代文档，作者成功为DEC Professional 380运行的PRO/VENIX系统开发了一个简易网络栈，通过SLIP和Crypto Ancienne代理实现对现代互联网的访问，并成功在真实硬件上加载Google主页。

文章还回顾了DEC Professional系列电脑的历史。DEC最初计划将Professional系列作为桌面办公电脑推出，避免与PDP-11小型计算机竞争，但因软件延迟发布而失败。随后，DEC改变策略，将Professional系列作为PDP-11桌面电脑销售，并移植了多个操作系统，包括基于V7和System V的PRO/VENIX。最终，DEC选择VenturCom的Venix作为官方Unix选项，而非自行开发的Ultrix-11，因为后者在性能上遇到问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在老旧计算机上实现网络协议的可行性及相关项目

不同观点：
• [trollbridge] 认为在老旧的PC上实现完整的网络协议栈（如SLIP、TCP/IP、SMTP、POP3）非常困难，尤其是在性能有限、内存受限的设备上。他通过自身经历说明了在PC BASIC环境下实现这些协议的挑战，包括字符丢失、计算校验和的困难以及内存限制等问题。尽管存在这些问题，他最终还是成功实现了基本功能。

• [jrdres] 指出将TCP/IP协议引入老旧机器是一个正在流行的趋势，并提到了一些现有的项目，如M Brutman的"mTCP"驱动和DogCow的"Sabina"网络套件，这些项目旨在为8088 PC和原始的128K Macintosh提供网络功能。他提到这些项目进展缓慢，部分原因是开发者的日常工作影响。

补充讨论：
• [pjmlp] 简短评论，认为这是一个有趣的历史片段，但没有深入讨论技术细节或表达明确立场。

争议焦点：
• 实现老旧计算机上的网络协议栈的可行性及其实际应用价值。 [trollbridge] 强调了技术挑战和实际困难，而 [jrdres] 则指出现有项目和趋势，表明这种努力是有价值且可行的。

43741849.article_content:
I had this grand idea many moons ago about writing up a TCP/IP stack for the Commodore 64, along with a lot of other people, and several of those people eventually did so before I even wrote a single opcode of 6502 assembly. For that purpose I had bought the box set of
TCP/IP Illustrated
(what would now be called the first edition prior to the 2011 update) for a hundred-odd bucks on sale which has now sat on my bookshelf, encased in its original shrinkwrap, for at least twenty years. It would be fun to put up the 4.4BSD data structures poster it came with but that would require opening it.
Fortunately, today
we have AI
we have many more excellent and comprehensive documents on the subject, and more importantly, we've recently brought back up an oddball platform that doesn't have networking either: our DEC Professional 380 running the System V-based PRO/VENIX V2.0, which you met
a couple articles back
. The DEC Professionals are a notoriously incompatible member of the PDP-11 family and, short of DECnet (DECNA) support in its unique Professional Operating System, there's officially no other way you can get one on a network — let alone the modern Internet. Are we going to let that stop us?
Of course not! Here's our barebones network stack for PRO/VENIX, the Pro's only official Unix option, downloading the Google home page on real hardware (internal addresses bleeped out) over SLIP and a
Crypto Ancienne
proxy for TLS 1.3. And, as we'll discuss, if you can get
this
thing on the network, you can get almost
anything
on the network! Easily portable and painfully verbose source code is included.
Recall from our lengthy history of
DEC's early misadventures with personal computers
that, in Digital's ill-advised plan to avoid the DEC Pros cannibalizing low-end sales from their categorical PDP-11 minicomputers, Digital's Small Systems Group deliberately made the DEC Professional series nearly totally incompatible despite the fact they used the same CPUs. In their initial roll-out strategy in 1982, the Pros (as well as their sibling systems, the Rainbow and the DECmate II) were only supposed to be mere desktop office computers — the fact the Pros were PDP-11s internally was mostly treated as an implementation detail. The idea backfired spectacularly against the IBM PC when the Pros and their promised office software failed to arrive on time and in 1984 DEC retooled around a new concept of explicitly selling the Pros as desktop PDP-11s. This required porting operating systems that PDP-11 minis typically ran: RSX-11M Plus was already there as the low-level layer of the Professional Operating System (P/OS), and DEC internally ported RT-11 (as PRO/RT-11) and COS.
PDP-11s were also famous for running Unix and so DEC needed a Unix for the Pro as well, though eventually only one official option was ever available: a port of VenturCom's Venix based on V7 Unix and later System V Release 2.0 called PRO/VENIX. After the
last article
, I had the distinct pleasure of being contacted by Paul Kleppner, the company's first paid employee in 1981, who was part of the group at VenturCom that did the Pro port and stayed at the company until 1988. Venix was originally developed from V6 Unix on the PDP-11/23 incorporating Myron Zimmerman's real-time extensions to the kernel (such as semaphores and asynchronous I/O), then a postdoc in physics at MIT; Kleppner's father was the professor of the lab Zimmerman worked in. Zimmerman founded VenturCom in 1981 to capitalize on the emerging Unix market, becoming one of the earliest commercial Unix licensees. Venix-11 was subsequently based on the later V7 Unix, as was Venix/86, which was the first Unix on the IBM PC in January 1983 and was ported to the DEC Rainbow as Venix/86R. In addition to its real-time extensions and enhanced segmentation capability, critical for memory management in smaller 16-bit address spaces, it also included a full desktop graphics package.
Notably, DEC themselves were also a Unix licensee through their Unix Engineering Group and already had an enhanced V7 Unix of their own running on the PDP-11, branded initially as V7M. Subsequently the UEG developed a port of 4.2BSD with some System V components for the VAX and planned to release it as Ultrix-32, simultaneously retconning V7M as Ultrix-11 even though it had little in common with the VAX release. Paul recalls that DEC did attempt a port of Ultrix-11 to the Pro 350 themselves but ran into intractable performance problems. By then the clock was ticking on the Pro relaunch and the issues with Ultrix-11 likely prompted DEC to look for alternatives. Crucially, Zimmerman had managed to upgrade Venix-11's kernel while still keeping it small, a vital aspect on his 11/23 which lacked split instruction and data addressing and would have had to page in and out a larger kernel otherwise. • [trollbridge] 认为在老旧的PC上实现完整的网络协议栈（如SLIP、TCP/IP、SMTP、POP3）非常困难，尤其是在性能有限、内存受限的设备上。他通过自身经历说明了在PC BASIC环境下实现这些协议的挑战，包括字符丢失、计算校验和的困难以及内存限制等问题。尽管存在这些问题，他最终还是成功实现了基本功能。

• [jrdres] 指出将TCP/IP协议引入老旧机器是一个正在流行的趋势，并提到了一些现有的项目，如M Brutman的"mTCP"驱动和DogCow的"Sabina"网络套件，这些项目旨在为8088 PC和原始的128K Macintosh提供网络功能。他提到这些项目进展缓慢，部分原因是开发者的日常工作影响。

• [pjmlp] 简短评论，认为这是一个有趣的历史片段，但没有深入讨论技术细节或表达明确立场。

争议焦点：
• 实现老旧计算机上的网络协议栈的可行性及其实际应用价值。 [trollbridge] 强调了技术挑战和实际困难，而 [jrdres] 则指出现有项目和趋势，表明这种努力是有价值且可行的。

data.title: 'Immediate red flags': questions raised over 'expert' much quoted in UK press
data.author: mellosouls
data.article_summary: 多家新闻机构，包括拥有《镜报》、《快报》和《星报》的Reach集团，正在撤下一位自称“心理学家和性咨询师”的芭芭拉·桑蒂尼（Barbara Santini）的相关报道。过去几年中，桑蒂尼被广泛引用，就疫情心理影响、维生素D重要性等话题发表看法。然而，她的资质受到质疑，英国心理学会（BPS）表示她并非其会员。调查显示，桑蒂尼的主要在线身份是性玩具网站Peaches and Screams的顾问，且其“牛津大学”背景无法验证。新闻机构如《每日星报》、《每日镜报》、《卫报》、BBC等已撤下她的评论。此事引发了对AI时代新闻来源验证的关注，一些平台开始改进专家验证机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新闻媒体如何核实信息来源及专家的资质，特别是在AI时代下信息真实性的挑战，以及媒体的可信度问题。

不同观点：
• [rurp] 对文章中的讽刺语气感到好笑，特别是对某人只有两个Medium粉丝的描述，认为这是种“笑里藏刀”的赞美。
• [sublimefire] 质疑某专家的资质，指出其声称的“牛津大学心理学家和性顾问”身份无法通过英国心理学会（BPS）验证，并担忧这种无法核实的情况可能导致任何人冒充专家。
• [duxup] 认为文章有趣，指出该‘人物’主要通过商业性网站和Medium存在，但在其他地方没有踪迹，并推测记者通过连接专家和记者的服务找到此人。
• [ern] 批评多家媒体的低质量，认为读者应具备批判性思维，辨别低质量内容，而不是盲目相信传统媒体或社交媒体上的信息。

Reach, which owns the Mirror, Express and Star, is among the news outlets removing Barbara Santini from its coverage,
Photograph: Yui Mok/PA
View image in fullscreen
Reach, which owns the Mirror, Express and Star, is among the news outlets removing Barbara Santini from its coverage,
Photograph: Yui Mok/PA
National newspapers
‘Immediate red flags’: questions raised over ‘expert’ much quoted in UK press
News outlets pull articles featuring ‘psychologist and sex adviser’ Barbara Santini amid doubts over her credentials
Michael Savage
Media editor
Sat 19 Apr 2025 04.14 EDT
Share
Over the past couple of years, the Oxford-educated psychologist Barbara Santini has been widely quoted as an expert. She has contributed thoughts on everything from the psychological impact of the Covid pandemic to the importance of vitamin D and how playing darts can improve your health.
However, her pronouncements have begun to disappear from articles after concerns that Santini may not be all that she appears. Major news outlets have removed entire articles featuring Santini, or comments made by her, after a series of questions were raised over her qualifications – and even whether her entire identity could be an elaborate hoax.
The case has been described as a wake-up call for newsrooms, as AI tools make it far easier for bad actors to invent supposed experts for their own purposes. Santini’s output has been prolific, with comments in Vogue, Metro, Cosmopolitan, the i newspaper, the Express, Hello!, the Telegraph, the Daily Star, the Daily Mail and the Sun in recent years. She was also quoted in an article for the BBC’s international site, BBC.com.
On closer inspection, her main online presence is as a sex and relationships adviser at an online sex toy outlet, Peaches and Screams. Some of the articles featuring her include a link to the store. Her qualifications are described there as “psychologist and sex adviser – University of Oxford”. However, the British Psychological Society (BPS) said she was not one of its members. She does not appear to have social media profiles, though she has two followers on the blogging site Medium.
Questions over Santini were first raised by the Press Gazette. Peaches and Screams did not respond to repeated requests for comment. The Guardian made several attempts to reach her through a number understood to be connected to her, asking for a meeting or conference call to confirm her identity as well as verification of her qualifications. A message was eventually received stating: “Thank you for your interest in this matter.” No further verification was provided.
Some of the reporters who have quoted her said they received comments through companies that connect journalists with experts. Some cited one such service, ResponseSource. The company has now launched an investigation and suspended the PR agency that handled Santini, and is planning a peer review system that allows journalists to rate an expert they have featured.
Santini also briefly featured on Qwoted, another platform connecting experts to journalists. Shelby Bridges, its director of user success, said the profile was removed after it found “immediate red flags pertaining to credentials and where the account was being accessed from”. She added: “Due to our inability to fully validate her credentials, we disabled the account shortly after it was created.”
Reach, which owns the Daily Mirror, Daily Express and Daily Star, is among the news outlets removing Santini from its coverage. This includes a Daily Star article in which Santini talked about how darts improved qualities such as “planning, foresight and problem-solving”.
Also removed was a Daily Mirror story in which Santini said the Covid pandemic had left some people with “difficulties establishing new relationships, heightened irritability, or a tendency to avoid social situations entirely”. The Guardian has removed her comments from an advertising feature on its website.
The BBC has removed her comments from a piece about AI by BBC Future, commissioned by BBC.com. A BBC spokesperson said: “As a widely used commentator, Barbara Santini’s quotes were used in good faith by BBC Future. While the substance of the article remains valid and her contribution was minor, given we have been unable to confirm Santini’s credentials, we have removed her quotes from the piece.”
The Independent has removed several stories that featured Santini commenting on subjects such as the differences between abuse and BDSM, as well as the importance of vitamin D. Yahoo has removed Santini’s quotes from articles, adding the clarification: “An earlier version of this story included information from a source whose expertise may not be valid. The quotes from the source have been removed.”
While the details of Santini’s case remain unclear, it has raised the issue of how journalists verify the credentials of sources in the AI age. Charlie Beckett, the leader of the journalism and AI project at the London School of Econ

data.title: Cheating the Reaper in Go
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何在Go语言中实现手动内存管理，尽管Go具有垃圾回收机制（GC）。作者通过构建一个无类型的、由GC管理的**arena**数据结构，展示了如何在纯Go中进行内存分配而不依赖runtime包。Go的设计避免了未定义行为（Undefined Behavior），并且GC的语义相对简单，使得这种操作成为可能。

作者首先解释了Go中`append`函数的工作原理，它通过指数增长动态数组来减少内存分配次数。而arena则是一种更通用的内存分配策略，它通过分配固定大小的内存块来提高效率。

文中展示了一个简单的内存分配器接口，并讨论了如何为其添加类型安全。然而，Go的GC还需要额外的类型信息，这带来了挑战。作者提醒读者，Go中的自定义分配器可能导致“使用已释放内存”的问题，因为GC在回收时无法识别自定义分配的内存。

总结来说，文章通过具体代码示例，探索了如何在Go中巧妙地绕过GC限制，实现高效的内存管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的内存管理与性能优化，特别是通过自定义分配器（arena allocator）和内存管理包来绕过垃圾回收（GC）以提升性能

不同观点：
• [silisili] 认为在使用Go进行性能调优时，可以通过自定义的arena设计（使用byte slices而不是unsafe指针）来优化性能。此外，他们提到可以通过预先更激进地增加容量来优化append操作，并提到unsafe.String可以有效减少不必要的内存分配。

• [fmstephe] 分享了自己开发的memorymanager包，该包通过绕过Go运行时的GC，手动管理内存分配，特别适用于构建零GC成本的大型长期数据结构（如内存缓存或数据库）。该包通过禁止指针类型并使用Reference[T]类型来实现类似功能，但需要手动释放内存。

Cheating the Reaper in Go
Even though I am a C++ programmer at heart, Go fascinates me for none of the reasons you think. Go has made several interesting design decisions:
It has virtually no Undefined Behavior
1
.
It has very simple GC semantics that they’re mostly stuck with due to design decisions in the surface language.
These things mean that despite Go having a GC, it’s possible to do manual memory management in pure Go and in cooperation with the GC (although without any help from the
runtime
package). To demonstrate this, we will be building an untyped, garbage-collected arena abstraction in Go which relies on several GC implementation details.
I would never play this kind of game in Rust or C++, because LLVM is extremely intelligent and able to find all kinds of ways to break you over the course of frequent compiler upgrades. On the other hand, although Go does not promise any compatibility across versions for code that imports
unsafe
, in practice, two forces work against Go doing this:
Go does not attempt to define what is and isn’t allowed:
unsafe
lacks any
operational semantics
.
Go prioritizes not breaking the ecosystem; this allows to assume that
Hyrum’s Law
will protect certain observable behaviors of the runtime, from which we may infer what can or cannot break easily.
This is in contrast to a high-performance native compiler like LLVM, which has a carefully defined boundary around all UB, allowing them to arbitrarily break programs that cross it (mostly) without fear of breaking the ecosystem.
So, let’s dive in and cheat death.
What Are We Building?
Our goal is to build an
arena
, which is a data structure for efficient allocation of memory that has the same lifetime. This reduces pressure on the general-purpose allocator by only requesting memory in large chunks and then freeing it all at once.

本文讨论了如何在Go语言中实现手动内存管理，尽管Go具有垃圾回收机制（GC）。作者通过构建一个无类型的、由GC管理的**arena**数据结构，展示了如何在纯Go中进行内存分配而不依赖runtime包。Go的设计避免了未定义行为（Undefined Behavior），并且GC的语义相对简单，使得这种操作成为可能。

作者首先解释了Go中`append`函数的工作原理，它通过指数增长动态数组来减少内存分配次数。而arena则是一种更通用的内存分配策略，它通过分配固定大小的内存块来提高效率。

文中展示了一个简单的内存分配器接口，并讨论了如何为其添加类型安全。然而，Go的GC还需要额外的类型信息，这带来了挑战。作者提醒读者，Go中的自定义分配器可能导致“使用已释放内存”的问题，因为GC在回收时无法识别自定义分配的内存。

总结来说，文章通过具体代码示例，探索了如何在Go中巧妙地绕过GC限制，实现高效的内存管理。

data.author: harryvederci
data.article_summary:
Evertop是一款超低功耗、超长电池寿命的太阳能便携电脑，仿IBM XT，搭载80186处理器和1MB内存，可运行DOS、Minix等1980年代操作系统，甚至支持Windows 3.0。它采用E-ink显示器，配备两块10,000mAh电池，并通过极端省电措施实现数百至数千小时的续航。内置太阳能板，可在离网情况下无限期使用。

设备包含丰富的内置外设，如内置键盘、PS/2接口、多种图形和音频支持、以太网和WiFi、LoRA无线电等。充电方式多样，包括太阳能板、DC输入和Micro USB。在省电模式下，续航可达200至500小时，甚至更长。

Evertop采用ESP32微控制器，5.83英寸648x480 E-ink显示屏，支持多系统启动和256GB SD卡存储，用于磁盘映像。设备还支持自动休眠和断电功能，以进一步节省电量。

Evertop: an ultra lower power, ultra long battery solar PC
Overview
Evertop is a portable PC that emulates an IBM XT with an 80186 processor and 1MB RAM. It can run DOS, Minix, and some other old 1980s operating systems.  It also runs Windows up to version 3.0.  Because it's based on a powerful yet very low power microcontroller, uses an e-ink display, packs two 10,000mAh batteries, and implements extreme power saving measures, it can run for hundreds or even thousands of hours on a single charge.  Combine that with its built in solar panel, and you should be able to use it indefinitely off grid without ever having to worry about battery life.
Loaded with built-in peripherals
It features a built in keyboard, external PS/2 keyboard and mouse ports, full CGA, Hercules, and MCGA graphics support, partial EGA and VGA support, PC speaker, Adlib, Covox, and Disney Sound Source audio output, built in speaker and headphone jack with volume control wheel, one DB9 RS232 serial port, one TTL serial port, dual keyboard and mouse PS/2 ports, USB flash drive port for convenient file transfer, an RJ45 ethernet port, wifi, and LoRA radio (I wrote a LoRA realtime chat client in QBASIC in about 15 minutes).  Bluetooth hardware is present but I have not yet implemented it in any features, though I plan to add support for BT keyboard and mouse, and maybe serial over BT, IP over BT, audio over BT, and BT file transfer.  The keyboard can be easily detached on a short tether to make it convenient to prop up the device at an angle while placing the keyboard on a flat surface.  Or you can just plug in your own to the PS/2 port, as sometimes it's nice to be able to use a full sized keyboard, though the one I built into this device is big enough for normal typing.
Charging options for every scenario
There are three ways you can power and charge this compputer: 1.) built in detachable solar panel, 2.) 2.5 - 20V DC input via an internal buck/boost circuit, or 3.) micro USB connector.  It can charge from all three sources simultaneously, and of course charge in every way while in use.  I also added a built in voltmeter to facilitate easy battery level and charge voltage monitoring.
Hundreds to thousands of hours on a single charge
In power saving mode it can run between 200 hours on the low side and 500 hours or in some cases even much longer of constant interactive use,
not
standby.  That should afford ample opportunity to find some sunny weather and recharge the batteries long before they start getting low.  I'm also going to port over a simple native (non-emulated) text editor / word processor and e-reader that I made several years ago for a similar pocket device.  I'm hoping I can get over 1000 hours of constant use on a single charge with those, maybe even 5000-10000 hours on the e-reader app.  Evertop also features optional user initiated or automatic hibernate to disk and automatic total power shutoff via an IO controlled dual MOSFET circuit, so you can set it to hibernate and it will completely shut off power when idle, then when you power back on you can resume right where yo left off.  Internal peripherals can be shut off when not in use via physical switches on the front panel to ensure no power is being wasted.  The solar panel is rated at 6V and 6W, so theoretically it should be able to produce 1 amp with full sunlight.  The most I've ever seen it do is 700mA, but even that's enough to provide ten to fifty hours of constant use from each hour of sunlight.  And even on the dimmest cloudy days it still gets around 70-100mA, which at least gives can give one to five hours of use per hour of charge.
Storage
I've been using a 256G SD card to store floppy and hard disk images, larger cards might work but I haven't tested one yet.  Hard drive images can be up to 4G each.  Emulated systems can mount two floppies and two hard drives for a total of 8G per emulated system.  You can set up multiple emulated systems and choose which one to boot at startup, or just default to the previous choice.
Technology
Under the hood it's powered by an Espressif ESP32 microcontroller.  The display is a 5.83 inch 648x480 (yes, 648 with the 8) "fast refresh" model from good-display.com which uses no power when not refreshing.  I started out using Fabrizio Di Vittorio's amazing and excellent PCEmu

• Bee_rider对硬件市场的看法：Bee_rider认为该硬件看起来可能会有市场，但对仿真老旧操作系统表示怀疑。
• Hyperhello对PowerBook 100仿真的建议：Hyperhello开玩笑地建议制作仿真PowerBook 100的设备。
• RecycledEle对便携电脑的评价：RecycledEle认为这就是便携电脑应有的样子。
• Karunamurti对DOOM的关注：Karunamurti幽默地表示对DOOM运行在设备上的关注。

评论中涉及多个技术细节和个人期望，包括显示屏寿命、CPU仿真、硬件节能、设备规格升级、太阳能CPU等。评论者对设备的功能和市场前景有不同的看法，有些人关注实际应用，有些人则更关注怀旧和趣味性。争议的焦点主要在于设备的仿真精度和硬件配置是否能够满足现代使用需求。

data.author: wilson090

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nvidia的市场地位及未来竞争格局

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为市场对Nvidia的悲观预测过多，且低估了Nvidia的竞争优势。尽管有人预测Nvidia将被竞争对手超越，但目前这些预测尚未实现。
• [ivape] 表示对Nvidia的看空观点不理解，认为Nvidia的硬件优势明显，且在多个新兴领域（如AI手机、自动驾驶汽车、机器人）具有竞争潜力。此外，提到Nvidia的生态系统强大，开发者对其有高度信仰。
• [lvl155] 怀疑AMD与Nvidia之间存在秘密合作，认为Nvidia在未来两年仍将主导市场，主要得益于其与苹果在TSMC的垄断地位。
• [Havoc] 认为Nvidia将从目前的功能性垄断转向更激烈的竞争环境，但这种转变不会对其造成致命打击。
• [alephnerd] 强调Nvidia可以通过服务和生态系统（如CUDA、Infiniband、NGC、NVLink等）来保护自己的市场地位，并建议通过扩展应用和咨询服务来应对市场变化。
• [echelon] 指出Nvidia目前享有定价权，但长期（超过6年）的可持续性存在疑问，特别是面对大型云服务商（如Google、Microsoft、Amazon、Meta）的自研芯片竞争。

补充讨论：
• [cornhole] 和 [ein0p] 就Nvidia的GPU驱动程序质量问题展开讨论。[cornhole] 认为Nvidia的QA（质量保证）有所下滑，而 [ein0p] 则反驳说Nvidia的产品一直供不应求，质疑质量问题是否存在。
• [mkoubaa] 提到，当类似评论出现在主流媒体（如Financial Times）时，自己会选择买入Nvidia股票，暗示对市场看空言论不以为然。

争议焦点：
• Nvidia的长期竞争优势是否会被大型云服务商的自研芯片和其他竞争对手削弱。
• Nvidia的GPU驱动程序质量是否在下降，尽管其产品供不应求。

总体来看，讨论围绕Nvidia的市场主导地位能否持续，以及面对竞争和技术变化，Nvidia应如何调整策略以保持其领先地位。

data.title: Ultra-precision formation flying demonstration for space-based interferometry
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为SILVIA（Space Interferometer Laboratory Voyaging towards Innovative Applications）的任务概念，旨在展示三艘航天器之间100米尺度上的超精密编队飞行。SILVIA目标是通过集成航天器传感器、激光干涉测量、低推力和低噪声微推进技术，实现亚微米级的相对距离控制，实时测量和控制航天器之间的距离和相对姿态。该任务设置在近地低轨道，平衡了相对扰动小和碰撞风险低的优势，为未来引力波观测台（如DECIGO）和直接成像系外行星热辐射的高对比度干涉仪（如LIFE）等任务奠定了技术基础。文章概述了任务概念及其关键技术，为下一代高精度太空观测站铺平道路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PROBA-3 任务及其技术应用的准确性和潜在用途

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为 PROBA-3 实现的亚毫米级相对位移精度和角秒级的指向精度令人惊讶，因为通常在射电干涉测量中，这种精度通常出现在更大距离（如公里级）的设置中。他质疑这种小尺度的精度是否有用，尤其是在光学干涉测量中可能有不同的需求。

• [ziofill] 从实验室光学干涉测量的难度出发，认为在卫星间实现如此高的对准精度是极其惊人的，因为即使在光学平台上，部件都是固定住的，而卫星则是在动态环境中操作。

• [aerostable_slug] 提出该技术可能具有双重用途，暗示其在军事领域中的应用，例如通过射频发射定位目标，类似于美国海军的 NOSS、法国的 CERES 以及中国的 Yaogan 卫星集群。

• [hydrogen7800] 提到 GRACE 任务已经使用类似的双卫星干涉测量技术来绘制重力异常图，表明这种技术并非全新，且已有成功应用的实例。

• [Animats] 认为该技术可用于恒星日冕仪以寻找太阳系外行星，通过遮挡恒星光线来观察行星。他提到喷气推进实验室（JPL）曾考虑过这种方法，但最终选择了更传统的设计。

• [londons_explore] 关注到大气密度变化对高空任务的影响，并提出通过飞得更高来解决这一问题，暗示大气条件可能是此类任务的限制因素。

补充讨论：
• PROBA-3 任务的技术挑战和创新性，尤其是在高精度对准和动态环境中实现高精度测量方面。
• 不同类型的干涉测量技术（射电、光学）在精度和距离上的差异，以及各自的应用场景。
• 该技术可能的军事应用和其他科学任务中的潜在用途。
• 大气条件对高空任务的影响及其解决方案。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We propose SILVIA (Space Interferometer Laboratory Voyaging towards Innovative Applications), a mission concept designed to demonstrate ultra-precision formation flying between three spacecraft separated by 100 m. SILVIA aims to achieve sub-micrometer precision in relative distance control by integrating spacecraft sensors, laser interferometry, low-thrust and low-noise micro-propulsion for real-time measurement and control of distances and relative orientations between spacecraft. A 100-meter-scale mission in a near-circular low Earth orbit has been identified as an ideal, cost-effective setting for demonstrating SILVIA, as this configuration maintains a good balance between small relative perturbations and low risk for collision. This mission will fill the current technology gap towards future missions, including gravitational wave observatories such as DECIGO (DECihertz Interferometer Gravitational wave Observatory), designed to detect the primordial gravitational wave background, and high-contrast nulling infrared interferometers like LIFE (Large Interferometer for Exoplanets), designed for direct imaging of thermal emissions from nearby terrestrial planet candidates. The mission concept and its key technologies are outlined, paving the way for the next generation of high-precision space-based observatories.

data.title: Business Cards
data.author: kolyder
data.article_summary: "Business Cards by Kolyder" 是一组以幽默讽刺职场文化的卡片，模仿策略、战斗和职场术语，反映出职场如战场的体验。卡片上充满自嘲和调侃，如“武器化的不称职”和“加上AI”等，反映职场中的无奈与荒谬。文章通过问答形式解答了关于卡片的常见问题，强调这并非真正的游戏，而是对职场的讽刺。同时，文章也展现出对自我和工作的调侃态度，适合在同事间分享以增添一丝娱乐。最终，卡片既是职场困境的反映，也是对作者童年兴趣的致敬。

Strategic execution. Hostile takeovers. Bullet points. Post-mortems.

What in the fresh hell is this?

Questions are not allowed during this meeting. Frankly, I'm not sure how you were unmuted.

Absolutely! Business Cards offer that perfect blend of potential unemployment and trivial amusement.

Almost certainly not. But you play the cards you’re delt.

Expand
If you do, we’ll report you for taking that sick day to snowboard last year.

The cards? No. Your career? Yes. Play on, my friend.

Expand
Depends. Are they chill? Do they have a sense of self-awareness?

As a child growing up in rural Nebraska, I spent many hours outdoors trying to conjure orbs with my mind. Naturally, I was inclined to like Magic: The Gathering.
I still spend a lot of time conjuring things with my mind. Not orbs, but marketing strategies for companies. I take my work seriously. Myself? Not so much. These Business Cards are an homage to something I enjoyed.

View a PDF of the paper titled Pydrofoil: accelerating Sail-based instruction set simulators, by Carl Friedrich Bolz-Tereick and Luke Panayi and Ferdia McKeogh and Tom Spink and Martin Berger
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present Pydrofoil, a multi-stage compiler that generates instruction set simulators (ISSs) from processor instruction set architectures (ISAs) expressed in the high-level, verification-oriented ISA specification language Sail. Pydrofoil shows a > 230x speedup over the C-based ISS generated by Sail on our benchmarks, and is based on the following insights. (i) An ISS is effectively an interpreter loop, and tracing just-in-time (JIT) compilers have proven effective at accelerating those, albeit mostly for dynamically typed languages. (ii) ISS workloads are highly atypical, dominated by intensive bit manipulation operations. Conventional compiler optimisations for general-purpose programming languages have limited impact for speeding up such workloads. We develop suitable domain-specific optimisations. (iii) Neither tracing JIT compilers, nor ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation alone, even with domain-specific optimisations, suffice for the generation of performant ISSs. Pydrofoil therefore implements a hybrid approach, pairing an AOT compiler with a tracing JIT built on the meta-tracing PyPy framework. AOT and JIT use domain-specific optimisations. Our benchmarks demonstrate that combining AOT and JIT compilers provides significantly greater performance gains than using either compiler alone.

data.title: 101 BASIC Computer Games
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了由maurymarkowitz整理的101个BASIC计算机游戏程序，这些程序来源于1975年出版的David Ahl的《101 BASIC Computer Games》一书。该集合包含了原始的DEC和Dartmouth方言编写的程序，与后来更著名的《BASIC Computer Games》（BCG）不同，两者包含的游戏和使用的BASIC方言有所不同。该集合展示了早期编程的多样性，如不同方言使用不同的语法和编程风格，例如使用`\`或`:`分隔语句，以及使用`&`代替`PRINT`等。这些程序大多通过OCR技术转换，并在RetroBASIC上运行良好，旨在提供示例代码以改进该程序。集合中的游戏示例包括ACEYDU、AMAZIN、ANIMAL、AWARI等，涵盖了不同的BASIC方言和玩法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕QBasic及相关老式编程游戏的讨论，包括对具体游戏缺失的遗憾、对老式代码的怀旧、如何运行这些老式游戏的可行建议以及对游戏质量的质疑。

不同观点：

• 一些用户表达了对QBasic经典游戏（如Nibbles、Gorilla）未包含在内的失望。例如，[zkmon]和[saneshark]提到他们希望看到这些游戏被包含，特别是Gorilla.bas曾是他们的最爱。

• [DigiEggz]分享了对阅读老游戏源码和语言描述的享受，认为过去的表达方式有独特魅力，并好奇是否有些 forgotten words 会重新流行。

• [vunderba]建议使用DOS模拟器如DosBox-X来运行QBasic游戏，并提到现代变种如QB64，但他个人认为从解释型语言转向编译型语言会失去很多原有的风味。

• [chasil]提到了不同平台上的BASIC变种，并列举了一些相关书籍和作者，展示了过去在多个平台上BASIC的广泛应用。

• [genghisjahn]和[jasperry]分享了他们对Amiga Basic和Commodore 64上BASIC编程的美好回忆，特别是无行号编程的新体验。

补充讨论：

• [dang]提供了一个相关的链接，关于更新“101 Basic Computer Games”以适应2021年的讨论，显示出这个话题有一定的延续性和关注度。

• [Narishma]质疑这些老游戏的质量是否值得关注，提出了对游戏可玩性的疑问。

• [khazhoux]以讽刺口吻建议将程序变成JPG格式让用户手动输入，暗示对现代便捷开发环境的反思。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在是否需要包含某些经典游戏如Gorilla.bas，以及老式BASIC游戏在现代是否仍有价值。

• 另一个小争议点是关于BASIC从解释型转向编译型的讨论，[vunderba]认为这会失去原有风味，而现代变种的支持者可能不这么认为。

101 BASIC Computer Games
This folder contains the programs found in the March 1975 3rd printing of David Ahl's
101 BASIC Computer Games
, published by Digital Equipment Corp. You can download all of the programs in a single archive using the
Releases
link to the right.
Contrary to popular belief, 101 is
not
the same as the later and more famous
BASIC Computer Games
(BCG) published by Ahl through Creative Computing. A number of the games in this collection did not appear in BCG, and vice versa. In comparison to BCG's used of Microsoft-like BASIC, the source in this book spans several different and sometimes incompatible dialects. For instance, CAN-AM is in its original Dartmouth version, and BATTLE appears to be HP 2100. In some cases the dialect is mentioned in the book, but in most it's not and the listing below is a best-guess based on the syntax.
This collection is an excellent example of the different dialects and programming styles one found at the time. ANIMAL is almost a different language than ACEYDU although they are both from DEC, while AWARI illustrates the editing style that made BASIC infamous. Even within the DEC examples we have differences in things like using
\
to separate statements instead of
:
, the use of
&
as the short form for
PRINT
instead of
?
, and the other oddities of BASIC-PLUS.
This collection was prepared with the help of the OCR in Gemini AI, ChatGTP and Le Chat. In contrast to other collections, like
PCC
, the print quality of this book is fairly good and most of the programs were converted with minimal problems. See the
NOTES
for some oddities to look for.
Many of these programs will run correctly without editing under
RetroBASIC
, and one of the reasons for creating this collection is to provide example code to improve that program.

• [wduquette] 认为《Crafting Interpreters》是他自20世纪70年代以来读过的最喜欢的编程书籍之一，称赞其清晰度和设计精良。
• [stefanos82] 也喜欢《Crafting Interpreters》，尤其欣赏作者Bob的写作风格和C语言实现，并表示对该书的偏爱。
• [greybox] 建议略读《Crafting Interpreters》的前几章，认为其核心价值在于递归下降算法和抽象语法树，其余部分则是实现细节。他还提到书中的例子是Java，但他自己使用了C++，并认为这些概念可以转移到Go等其他语言。
• [Spartan-S63] 读过《Writing an Interpreter in Go》和《Writing a Compiler in Go》，认为这些书是入门解析器和编译器主题的极好资源，并表示希望有更多机会练习解析器编写。虽然《Crafting Interpreters》还在阅读计划中，但根据各方评价，它也是一本出色的书籍。
• [SwiftyBug] 正在用Go实现《Crafting Interpreters》中的内容，认为将书中的OOP实现“翻译”为更符合Go语言习惯的实现是一个有趣的练习。
• [markus_zhang] 只读过《Crafting Interpreters》并推荐它，提到该书有免费的在线版本，可以先评估再购买。
• [angra_mainyu] 开始读一些相关书籍但放弃了，选择了《Engineering a Compiler》、《Programming Language Pragmatics》和《Crafting a Compiler》，认为如果专注于一本书并辅以其他两本，是可以完成的。

• 《Crafting Interpreters》被广泛称赞为清晰且设计精良，适合不同背景的读者。

• [greybox] 建议略读《Crafting Interpreters》的前几章，认为其核心价值在于递归下降算法和抽象语法树，其余部分则是实现细节。他还提到书中的例子是Java，但他自己使用了C++，并认为这些概念可以转移到Go等其他语言。
• [Spartan-S63] 读过《Writing an Interpreter in Go》和《Writing a Compiler in Go》，认为这些书是入门解析器和编译器主题的极好资源，并表示希望有更多机会练习解析器编写。虽然《Crafting Interpreters》还在阅读计划中，但根据各方评价，它也是一本出色的书籍。
• [SwiftyBug] 正在用Go实现《Crafting Interpreters》中的内容，认为将书中的OOP实现“翻译”为更符合Go语言习惯的实现是一个有趣的练习。
• [markus_zhang] 只读过《Crafting Interpreters》并推荐它，提到该书有免费的在线版本，可以先评估再购买。
• [angra_mainyu] 开始读一些相关书籍但放弃了，选择了《Engineering a Compiler》、《Programming Language Pragmatics》和《Crafting a Compiler》，认为如果专注于一本书并辅以其他两本，是可以完成的。

补充讨论：
• 《Crafting Interpreters》被广泛称赞为清晰且设计精良，适合不同背景的读者。
• 不同读者根据自己的语言偏好（如Go、C++）对书中的实现进行了调整和应用。
• 有读者提到其他相关书籍如《Writing an Interpreter in Go》、《Writing a Compiler in Go》和《Engineering a Compiler》等，并比较了它们的优缺点。
• 一些读者强调了《Crafting Interpreters》中概念的通用性，认为可以应用于不同编程语言。
• 书籍的可访问性也被提及，例如《Crafting Interpreters》有免费的在线版本供评估。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用**Immortal**工具在多种操作系统（如macOS、FreeBSD、OpenBSD、NetBSD、Linux）上管理和监控服务进程。Immortal可以跟踪进程ID（PID）、记录日志、处理重试机制，并通过配置文件（如`run.yml`）进行设置。文章还提到了如何处理标准错误输出（stderr）以及结合Nginx使用。此外，文章展示了如何使用Ansible playbook示例来管理Immortal，并详细说明了如何安装和设置Immortal，包括使用`dpkg`命令安装软件包、通过Systemd管理服务，以及利用配置文件如`immortaldir.service`和`service.yml`等。手册页如`man immortal(8)`、`man immortalctl(8)`和`man immortaldir(8)`提供了进一步的帮助。

data.title: Columbia student suspended over interview cheating tool raises $5.3M
data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: 21岁的Chungin "Roy" Lee及其创业公司Cluely获得了530万美元的种子轮融资，投资方包括Abstract Ventures和Susa Ventures。Cluely提供一种“作弊工具”，利用隐藏的浏览器窗口帮助用户在考试、销售电话和面试中作弊。该创业公司源于Lee和另一位哥伦比亚大学学生Neel Shanmugam开发的面试作弊工具，他们因此被学校停学，随后辍学。Cluely声称其工具类似于计算器和拼写检查，最初被批评为作弊，但现已实现超过300万美元的年经常性收入。尽管其宣传视频引发争议，有人将其比作反乌托邦剧集“黑镜”，Cluely仍坚持推广其AI作弊工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术岗位面试中的新兴工具及其影响，特别是AI工具对招聘过程的潜在作用和争议

不同观点：
• ryandrake：支持任何能取代当前高压面试方式（如LeetCode测验、白板题、高压力编程挑战等）的工具，认为现有面试流程对求职者来说如同噩梦，但并未提出具体解决方案。
• quantified：关注面试工具的隐私问题，指出根据隐私政策，工具会与第三方分享捕获的音频和屏幕截图，可能侵犯个人隐私，类似于微软Recall但更具吸引力。
• esel2k：认为这种趋势将推动更多的合同工转正模式，公司会先以合同工形式试用人员，如果不符合预期就解雇。同时提到公司可以选择恢复面对面面试或其他方法。
• pogue：质疑是否很难在求职者自己的显示器上保留一些“不可检测”的内容，认为如果只是一个AI聊天机器人，主动监听或阅读屏幕且仅对一方可见，似乎很容易实现。
• NoTeslaThrow：提到曾发现有人使用AI作弊，认为如果通过AI能绕过关键词招聘和不称职的招聘人员，愿意为此付费。同时指出具有工程背景的招聘人员在识别候选人方面更有价值。
• mattfrommars：讽刺UI/UX设计是否展示了530万美元的效果，质疑新技术是否物有所值。
• horns4lyfe：认为如果面试流程已经 broken 到可以通过AI作弊获得工作，那么这个行业就是在进行“底线竞赛”，表示想要转行。

补充讨论：
• Centigonal：简短评论，认为这是典型的2025年硅谷现象，暗示对新技术趋势的怀疑态度。

争议焦点：
• AI工具在技术招聘中的使用及其对公平性的影响：一方面有人支持AI工具能改善面试体验，另一方面担心AI作弊和隐私问题。

43757209.article_content:
On Sunday, 21-year-old Chungin “Roy” Lee
announced
he’s raised $5.3 million in seed funding from Abstract Ventures and Susa Ventures for his startup, Cluely, that offers an AI tool to “cheat on everything.”
The startup was born after Lee
posted
in a viral X thread that he was suspended by Columbia University after he and his co-founder developed a tool to cheat on job interviews for software engineers.
That tool, originally called Interview Coder, is now part of their San Francisco-based startup
Cluely
. It offers its users the chance to “cheat” on things like exams, sales calls, and job interviews thanks to a hidden in-browser window that can’t be viewed by the interviewer or test giver.
Cluely has published
a manifesto
comparing itself to inventions like the calculator and spellcheck, which were originally derided as “cheating.”
Cluely also published a slickly produced, but polarizing, launch video of Lee using a hidden AI assistant to (unsuccessfully) lie to a woman about his age, and even his knowledge of art, on a date at a fancy restaurant:
Cluely is out. cheat on everything.
pic.twitter.com/EsRXQaCfUI
— Roy (@im_roy_lee)
April 20, 2025
While some
praised
the video for grabbing people’s attention, others derided it as reminiscent of the dystopian sci-fi television show “Black Mirror”:
Imagine making a black mirror short as a product ad
https://t.co/2GKXQj8e1v
— Cody Blakeney (@code_star)
April 21, 2025
Lee, who is Cluely’s CEO, told TechCrunch the AI cheating tool surpassed $3 million in ARR earlier this month.
The startup’s other co-founder is another 21-year-old former Columbia student, Neel Shanmugam, who is Cluely’s COO. Shanmugam was also embroiled in disciplinary proceedings at Columbia over the AI tool. Both co-founders have dropped out of Columbia, the university’s student newspaper
reported
last week. Columbia declined to comment, citing student privacy laws.
Cluely began as a tool for developers to cheat on knowledge of LeetCode, a platform for coding questions that some in software engineering circles — including Cluely’s founders, of course — consider outdated and a waste of time.
Lee says he was able to snag an internship with Amazon using the AI cheating tool. Amazon declined to comment on Lee’s particular case to TechCrunch, but said its job candidates must acknowledge they won’t use unauthorized tools during the interview process.
Cluely isn’t the only controversial AI startup launched this month. Earlier, a famed AI researcher announced his own startup with the
stated mission of replacing all human workers everywhere
, causing a brouhaha of its own on X.

data.title: NASA’s Lucy Spacecraft Images Asteroid Donaldjohanson
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: NASA的露西号航天器在2025年4月20日近距离飞越了唐纳德约翰森小行星，拍摄到这颗形成于约1.5亿年前的独特形状小行星图像。唐纳德约翰森小行星呈细长接触双星状，两端由细颈连接，形似两个嵌套的冰淇淋锥。初步分析显示，小行星长约8公里，最宽处约3.5公里，比最初估计的要大。露西号的L’LORRI相机拍摄的高分辨率图像将帮助科学家研究小行星的复杂结构，揭示太阳系行星的构建模块和碰撞过程。虽然唐纳德约翰森小行星并非露西任务的主要科学目标，但此次飞越是任务的全面演练，旨在最大化数据收集。露西号将继续在2025年穿越主小行星带，并计划于2027年8月抵达其首个木星特洛伊小行星目标。

4 min read
NASA’s Lucy Spacecraft Images Asteroid Donaldjohanson
NASA Science Editorial Team
Apr 21, 2025
Image Article
In its second asteroid encounter, NASA’s Lucy spacecraft obtained a close look at a uniquely shaped fragment of an asteroid that formed about 150 million years ago. The spacecraft has begun returning images that were collected as it flew approximately 600 miles (960 km) from the asteroid Donaldjohanson on April 20, 2025.
The asteroid Donaldjohanson as seen by the Lucy Long-Range Reconnaissance Imager (L’LORRI) on NASA’s Lucy spacecraft during its flyby. This timelapse shows images captured approximately every 2 seconds beginning at 1:50 p.m. EDT (17:50 UTC), April 20, 2025. The asteroid rotates very slowly; its apparent rotation here is due to the spacecraft’s motion as it flies by Donaldjohanson at a distance of 1,000 to 660 miles (1,600 to 1,100 km). The spacecraft’s closest approach distance was 600 miles (960 km), but the images shown were taken approximately 40 seconds beforehand, the nearest ones at a distance of 660 miles (1100 km).
NASA/Goddard/SwRI/Johns Hopkins APL
The asteroid was previously observed to have large brightness variations over a 10-day period, so some of Lucy team members’ expectations were confirmed when the first images showed what appeared to be an elongated contact binary (an object formed when two smaller bodies collide). However, the team was surprised by the odd shape of the narrow neck connecting the two lobes, which looks like two nested ice cream cones.
“Asteroid Donaldjohanson has strikingly complicated geology,” says Hal Levison, principal investigator for Lucy at Southwest Research Institute, Boulder, Colorado. “As we study the complex structures in detail, they will reveal important information about the building blocks and collisional processes that formed the planets in our Solar System.”
From a preliminary analysis of the first available images collected by the spacecraft's L’LORRI imager, the asteroid appears to be larger than originally estimated, about 5 miles (8 km) long and 2 miles (3.5 km) wide at the widest point. In this first set of high-resolution images returned from the spacecraft, the full asteroid is not visible as the asteroid is larger than the imager’s field of view. It will take up to a week for the team to downlink the remainder of the encounter data from the spacecraft; this dataset will give a more complete picture of the asteroid’s overall shape.
Like Lucy’s first asteroid flyby target, Dinkinesh, Donaldjohanson is not a primary science target of the Lucy mission. As planned, the Dinkinesh flyby was a system’s test for the mission, while this encounter was a full dress rehearsal, in which the team conducted a series of dense observations to maximize data collection. Data collected by Lucy’s other scientific instruments, the L’Ralph color imager and infrared spectrometer and the L’TES thermal infrared spectrometer, will be retrieved and analyzed over the next few weeks.
The Lucy spacecraft will spend most of the remainder of 2025 travelling through the main asteroid belt. Lucy will encounter the mission’s first main target, the Jupiter Trojan asteroid Eurybates, in August 2027.
“These early images of Donaldjohanson are again showing the tremendous capabilities of the Lucy spacecraft as an engine of discovery,” said Tom Statler, program scientist for the Lucy mission at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “The potential to really open a new window into the history of our solar system when Lucy gets to the Trojan asteroids is immense.”
The asteroid Donaldjohanson as seen by the Lucy Long-Range Reconnaissance Imager (L’LORRI). This is one of the most detailed images returned by NASA’s Lucy spacecraft during its flyby. This image was taken at 1:51 p.m. EDT (17:51 UTC), April 20, 2025, near closest approach, from a range of approximately 660 miles (1,100 km). The spacecraft’s closest approach distance was 600 miles (960 km), but the image shown was taken approximately 40 seconds beforehand. The image has been sharpened and processed to enhance contrast.
NASA/Goddard/SwRI/Johns Hopkins APL/NOIRLab
NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, provides overall mission management, systems engineering and the safety and mission assurance for Lucy, as well as the designing and building the L’Ralph instrument. Hal Levison of the Boulder, Colorado, office of SwRI is the principal investigator. SwRI is headquartered in San Antonio and also leads the mission's science team, science observation planning, and data processing. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, provides overall mission management, systems engineering, and the safety and mission assurance for Lucy, as well as the L’Ralph instrument. Lockheed Martin Space in Littleton, Colorado, built the spacecraft, designed the orbital trajectory, and provides flight operations. Goddard and KinetX Aerospace are responsible for navigating the Lucy spacecraft. Th
43757130.article_summary: NASA的露西号航天器在2025年4月20日近距离飞越了唐纳德约翰森小行星，拍摄到这颗形成于约1.5亿年前的独特形状小行星图像。唐纳德约翰森小行星呈细长接触双星状，两端由细颈连接，形似两个嵌套的冰淇淋锥。初步分析显示，小行星长约8公里，最宽处约3.5公里，比最初估计的要大。露西号的L’LORRI相机拍摄的高分辨率图像将帮助科学家研究小行星的复杂结构，揭示太阳系行星的构建模块和碰撞过程。虽然唐纳德约翰森小行星并非露西任务的主要科学目标，但此次飞越是任务的全面演练，旨在最大化数据收集。露西号将继续在2025年穿越主小行星带，并计划于2027年8月抵达其首个木星特洛伊小行星目标。

data.title: Deus Lex Machina: releasing a new compacting Zig tokenizer
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary:
文章宣布了一个全新的、紧凑的Zig语言 tokenizer 的 alpha 版本发布，该工具可以显著提高 tokenizing 速度，目前支持 AMD64 架构的机器，并使用 AVX-512 指令集。该实现比标准库中的 tokenizer 快 2.75 倍，速度达到 1.4GB/s，且内存消耗减少了 2.47 倍。

该 tokenizer 使用了 SIMD 技术，通过并行处理 64 字节（未来将扩展到 512 字节）的代码块，实现了包括 UTF-8 验证、无分支位操作、向量查找表等多项优化。它几乎完全通过位操作和 SIMD 操作实现 token 匹配，避免了不必要的分支，从而提高了性能。

文章还提供了基准测试结果，显示新 tokenizer 在处理文件速度和内存使用上的显著优势。通过处理整个数据块并行查找 token 边界，该工具实现了高速的 tokenizing 过程。

Deus Lex Machina
2025-04-16
+
simd

tokenizer
Today, I am excited to announce the alpha release of a brand new compacting Zig tokenizer! You may find it in the following repository:
Validark
/
Accelerated-Zig-Parser
Waiting for api.github.com...
00K
0K
0K
Waiting...
Give it a star and come back!
Please note it is not ready for prime-time just yet, since there are still more optimizations to be had, as well as support for more architectures.
At the moment, only AMD64 machines with AVX-512 instructions are supported.
That being said, the new implementation can tokenize up to
2.75x faster
than the mainline implementation, currently at
1.4GB/s
on a single core on my laptop, with a lot of improvements coming soon!
All Your Tokens Are Belong to Us
§
The above repository benchmarks 3 Zig tokenizers:
The tokenizer in the Zig Standard Library used by the 0.14 compiler.
A heat-seeking tokenizer (
talk 1
,
talk 2
)
(had to temporarily remove it, but will add back by July)
A
compacting tokenizer
(
talk 3
)
Benchmark results on my laptop with a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370:
Read in files in 26.479ms (1775.63 MB/s) and used 47.018545MB memory with 3504899722 lines across 3253 files
Legacy Tokenizing took              91.419ms (0.51 GB/s, 38.34B loc/s) and used 40.07934MB memory
Tokenizing with compression took    33.301ms (1.41 GB/s, 105.25B loc/s) and used 16.209284MB memory
That's 2.75x faster and 2.47x less memory than the mainline implementation!
Headline features
§
The new
compacting tokenizer
processes an entire 64-byte chunk of source code at once (soon to be 512!). It includes:
A fully SIMDized
UTF-8 validator
ported from
simdjson
/
simdutf
.
A fully branchless bit-manipulation routine to
determine which characters are escaped by backslashes
. (Thanks to John Keiser (@jkeiser) for
designing this algorithm for simdjson
.)
A loop which
parses all lines in a given chunk in parallel for strings/comments/character_literals/line_strings
. Characters inside of these constructs must be exempted from comprising their own tokens.
A multi-purpose vectorized table-lookup
. It performs Vectorized-Classification (making it so we can produce a bitstring of any group of characters we care about in one additional instruction), as well as mapping all characters that may appear in a multi-char symbol into a range of [0, 15] while everything else is mapped into the range [128, 255]. Cognoscenti would recognize this as matching the semantics of a
vpshufb
instruction. It also is itself a mostly-correct vector of
kinds
fields (one of the pieces of information we need to output for each token).
A mini non-deterministic finite state machine
implemented using
vpshufb
instructions on the result of the vectorized table-lookup for multi-char-symbol matching, as well as an effectively-branchless (for real code)
reconciliation loop
which accepts bitstrings indicating where valid 2 and 3 character multi-char symbols end and deleting the ones that are impossible due to overlap.
SIMD hasher of up to 16 multi-char symbols at once
, which works across chunk boundaries to produce the proper
kind
of multi-char symbols.
A fully vectorized cross-chunk keyword hasher and validator
that pulls from a
common superstring
holding all keywords in a total of 4 64-byte vectors.
vpgather
instructions are not used.
Token-matching logic implemented almost entirely using bit-manipulation and SIMD operations
, the things CPU’s are the fastest at.
Logic void of almost all branches— they are only used where they provide a performance benefit.

§

data.author: ethn
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了世界正面临一场由技术引发的深刻变革，称之为“Spooner革命”。文章提到，尽管一些思想家如福山的学生认为历史已经终结，世界进入了停滞状态，但实际上，技术，尤其是人工智能（AI），正在推动一场比工业革命更剧烈的社会经济变革。自2017年提出“注意力机制”以来，AI模型如GPT通过不断增加数据处理量提升性能，但近期新模型的出现带来了质的飞跃，能够自动化包括设计、编辑、工程和分析等众多知识型工作。这种变革不仅限于工作安全问题，而是对整个社会经济结构的颠覆。文章警告，过去对自动化取代工作的预测过于保守，未考虑到最新AI技术的快速发展及其深远影响。

Back to all posts
The World Is Ending. Welcome to the Spooner Revolution.
April 18, 2025
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
The world is ending.
In the periphery enlightened Fukuyama acolytes readily worship the superstition that we've arrived at the fabled end of historyâthat immortal Zeitgeist, an eternal stasis. Online these committed worshipers believe that no more significant milestones in history will occur, the tapestry is woven. No more cloth is left to be added and if you can find a pair of scissors its edge is too dull to cut. They engage in a constant procession of scouring headlines for glimpses of evidence, of wellâ¦nothing happening, to proselytize that ostensible truth. They self-identify as "chuds", instead of being draped in robes they adorn a caricature of a bored unimpressed bespectacled teenager who behind his frown yearns for the promises of adventure from his childhood.
The Nothing Ever Happens Chudjak meme
It's easy to be sympathetic to this view, to be so impressed by the incredible structure of Capitalism as it emanates and petrifies throughout our constant world at a scale beyond the human grasp or intention. In a way they are right, organizations at any scale are tautologically negentropic. In another way, we should hope so, entropy is largely precarious. But if you look closely, cracks in their idols grow, soon to be swallowed whole.
Who is this phantom iconoclast? It's neither a capricious United States administration nor an economic powder keg but instead the usual suspect in real violent paradigmatic shifts: technology. We are at the precipice of a revolution more violent than the Industrial Revolution. This revolution is not about the typical vulgar parochial anxieties on job securityâalthough it is part of itâit's about a violent upheaval of the very socio-economic fabric in the way our world is organized.
Artificial Intelligence in the form of General Purpose Transformers since the 2017 seminal paper "Attention is All You Need"
1
was well understood to only provide achievement in degree to the extent of the quantity of data that could be processed. Even with that, there are obvious limitations described by Amdahl's law, which states there is a logarithmic maximum potential improvement by increasing hardware provisions. To further discourage AI researchers OpenAI themselves released a paper on the logarithmic gain of performance with the increased count of parameters "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners," Brown et al 2020
2
. Theoretically this inflection point was hit with ChatGPT-3.5+.
GPTs purported sublinear gains in the CoQA reading comprehension task as parameters increase
Yet despite their own publications, OpenAI continued to release new models albeit with the expected modest performance gains. However, recently a new class of models with unknown technical details from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have indisputably resulted in a zero-to-one improvement. This may be a result solely by respecting Chinchilla law but regardless of the particular innovation, they're not slowing down.
Historically, a steady supply of automation studies provided fodder for AI skepticism. In 2003, Autor et al had determined that only 2 out of 200 tasks could be automated in jobs.
Our analysis suggests that only a small fraction of tasks within a typical jobâon the order of 1 to 2 out of roughly 200 discrete tasksâcan be fully automated by existing classification algorithms and rule-based computer systems. The vast majority of tasks require tacit knowledge, judgment, and flexibility that remain beyond the reach of current automation technologies.
The latest MIT CSAIL study maintains that tasks responsible for 23% of wages will be completely automated.
3
According to Thompson, only 23% of the wages paid to humans for performing vision tasks would be economically attractive to automate with AI. The study underscores that, even with rapid decreases in AI costs, it would take decades for computer vision tasks to become economically efficient for firms
A 2025 WEF study suggests 39% of tasks will be completely 'replaced or transformed'
4
.
The current corpus encourages a rather provocative but treacly perspective on artificial intelligence. It's tempting to satiate the desire for consolation by wringing this data above the parched palate however all these studies were conducted before the release of these latest series of models and none account for any LLM technology. The latest innovations go far beyond logarithmic gains: there is now GPT-based software which replaces much of the work of CAD Designers, Illustrators, Video Editors, Electrical Engineers, Software Engineers, Financial Analysts, and Radiologists, to name a few. This radical automation exists without any sophisticated fine tuning or training. And yet these perinatal automatons are totally eviscerating all knowledge based work as the relaxation of the original hysterics arriv

data.title: Visiting – Epic
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: Epic Systems Corporation的总部位于威斯康星州维罗纳的乡村，距离麦迪逊市约11英里。游客需提前预约自助游览，总部有六个独特园区，包括大草原、中央公园、农场、学习、巫师学院和故事书园区，每个游览约需一小时。游客可在周末上午10点至下午3点，或平日下午2点至5点进行游览，团队人数有限制。部分园区如农场和故事书园区需经过其他园区才能到达。工作人员使用牛形自行车或车辆在园区内移动。若在关闭时间前接近完成游览，可继续完成。总部在特定日期不开放，需查看日历。麦迪逊市区也有丰富的文化和餐饮活动可探索。

We're located in the beautiful countryside of Verona, Wisconsin, about 11 miles southwest of Madison, the state capital.
We welcome registered visitors to our Intergalactic Headquarters during specific times throughout the week and on weekends. Stop by our reception desk during your pre-scheduled time slot to pick up a map for a self-guided tour. As you explore, you may encounter magic on our Wizards campus, see some familiar faces on our Storybook campus, or even encounter some furry friends on our functioning farm.
View the Epic fact sheet
→
We have six unique campuses for you to explore: the Prairie, Central Park, Farm, Learning, Wizards Academy, and Storybook campuses. Each tour takes about an hour. To get to the Farm campus, you’ll also get to enjoy the Prairie campus. For the Storybook and Wizards Academy campuses, you’ll start with the Central Park campus or take an expedited route to where those tours begin.
Staff use cow bikes, cow carts, or cow vans to
mooove
across campus.
Self-Guided Tours
Schedule a Tour
→
Sat-Sun | 10am - 3pm
Mon-Fri | 2pm - 5pm
Tour sizes are limited to groups of seven or fewer on weekdays and twelve or fewer on weekends.
Once on campus, follow the signs for visitors, and park in the visitor lot (under the solar panels).
If you are nearly done with a tour at closing time, please feel free to complete the campus you are on before leaving.
Tour Scheduling Required
You must make a reservation in advance to enjoy a self-guided tour of our campus. To check availability and sign up, click the Schedule a Tour button above. If you are unable to schedule a tour online, please give us a call. If you arrive on campus without a scheduled tour, we’ll be happy to help you sign up for any available slots on the spot, or reschedule for another time if there’s no availability.

data.title: Court Permanently Enjoins Ohio's Segregate-and-Suppress/Parental Consent Law
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 本文总结了俄亥俄州一项要求网站在允许未成年人访问特定功能前获得父母同意的法律被永久禁止的案件。法院认为该法律对未成年人的言论自由构成不当限制，特别是在社交媒体上。法院强调，未成年人接触信息对其成长至关重要，而社交媒体在提供社交联系和心理健康支持方面有积极作用，但也带来负面影响。法院指出，该法律在每次应用时都引发相同的宪法第一修正案问题，即它限制了运营者和未成年人的言论自由。最终，法院永久禁止该法律的实施，预计该案将上诉至第六巡回法院。作者还指出，强制年龄验证本质上对未成年人、成年人和出版方都有害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体运营者与传统出版者的内容管理责任比较

不同观点：
• [TimorousBestie的观点] 认为将社交媒体运营者的内容管理与传统出版者的例子相比较是不恰当的。他们指出，即使是进行轻度管理的出版者，也在做出与重度管理类似的编辑选择，只是不同程度的管理代表了不同的选择，而非优劣之分。此外，他们强调，法院例子中的报纸（如仅刊登读者来信的报纸）和社交媒体网站在管理范围上有质的区别。社交媒体网站通常没有一个编辑委员会在内容发布前明确批准内容，可能除了像Lobsters这样的特殊例子。

• [暗示的观点：hn_acker] 通过提供文章的完整标题，将讨论引向一个具体的法律案例（“法院永久禁止俄亥俄州的隔离和压制/父母同意法–NetChoice诉Yost”），暗示社交媒体内容管理可能与法律和监管问题相关。虽然未直接表达立场，但通过标题引导讨论向法律判决和其对社交媒体管理的影响方向发展。

补充讨论：
• TimorousBestie强调了社交媒体与传统出版者在内容管理上的结构性差异，特别是编辑委员会的存在与否和事前审核的差异。
• 提及Lobsters作为一个可能的例外，表明在社交媒体中可能存在不同的管理模式，值得进一步探讨。
• hn_acker的标题暗示法律对社交媒体内容管理的潜在影响，这可能涉及言论自由与内容审核之间的平衡问题。

争议焦点：社交媒体运营者是否应被视为与传统出版者具有相同的内容管理责任，以及不同程度的内容管理是否存在优劣之分。

43757325.article_content:
Court Permanently Enjoins Ohio’s Segregate-and-Suppress/Parental Consent Law–NetChoice v. Yost
April 21, 2025
· by
Eric Goldman
· in
Content Regulation
,
Licensing/Contracts
Ohio enacted a
segregate-and-suppress law
that requires regulated websites to obtain parental consent before minors can access certain site features. In early 2024, the
court granted a preliminary injunction
against the law going into effect. Borrowing heavily from its prior opinion, the court has now granted the permanent injunction. This tees up the case for its inevitable appeal to the Sixth Circuit.
Overview Remarks
The court notes the tensions around allowing children to access social media:
“Minors’ access to information is essential to their growth into productive members of our democratic public sphere”
“There are a number of good things to be said about social media platforms…The ability to form and to maintain social connections on these online platforms can have positive effects on children and adolescents, especially those who routinely feel marginalized or excluded. In addition to enabling peer connection and social support, social media can also promote positive and identity-affirming content and encourage behaviors that proactively address mental health care.”
“these benefits come with a cost. Extensive social media use also has been linked to higher rates of depression, anxiety, and loneliness among young people.”
Striking a balance between these considerations is a challenge: “lawmakers across the nation have sought to regulate online entities and cabin their deleterious effects, particularly on the youth. The task is an admittedly daunting one: Legislatures must craft laws broad enough to accommodate the pace with which digital platforms evolve, but not so broad that they cripple innovation or trample free speech.” I don’t think legislatures can find any constitutional way of navigating this dilemma given the perniciousness of mandatory age authentication.
Can NetChoice Bring a Facial Challenge?
The court says Ohio’s law is amenable to a facial First Amendment challenge:
in every application to a covered website, the Act raises the same First Amendment issues. Specifically, whether it is a NetChoice member product—YouTube; Facebook and Instagram; X; Nextdoor; Pinterest; or Dreamwidth—or other covered websites that provide the “socially interactive” features outlined in the Act and considered to be “target[ing]” minors or likely to be accessed by minors—like Goodreads, Soundcloud, Substack, Yelp, or LinkedIn—they are all are under the same statutory obligation to block access to unemancipated Ohio minors absent parental consent
From my perspective, mandatory age authentication always should be subject to a facial challenge because it always categorically harms minors, adults, and publishers, regardless of the perniciousness of the suppression obligation.
Does the Act Impact Protected Speech?
The court says
the Act’s First Amendment implications come into focus when social media operators are thought of as publishers of opinion work—a newspaper limited to “Letters to the Editor,” or a publisher of a series of essays by different authors. The analogy is an imperfect one—social media operators are arguably less involved in the curation of their websites’ content than these traditional examples. But the comparison helps clarify that the Act regulates speech in two consequential ways: (1) it regulates operators’ ability to publish and distribute speech to minors and speech by minors; and (2) it regulates minors’ ability both to produce speech and to receive speech….
These principles control here. The Act impedes minors’ ability to engage in and access speech by requiring covered websites to obtain parental consent before allowing any unemancipated child under the age of sixteen to register or create an account on their website. That means minors’ ability to contribute or access “a wide array of protected First Amendment activity on any number of diverse topics,” will be contingent on securing parental consent—an impermissible curtailment of their First Amendment rights.
I disagree with this characterization: “social media operators are arguably less involved in the curation of their websites’ content than these traditional examples.” A publisher who engages in light curation is making just as much of an editorial choice as those who engage in heavier curation. There’s not a “better” or “worse” level of curation; there are just different choices along a continuum. I also think the
Moody decision
clearly validated the protected editorial nature of social media services’ curation.
As I explain in my Segregate-and-Suppress paper, parental consent requirements are conditional access restrictions (i.e., conditioned on the parental consent). If parents say no, then the restriction becomes categorical for those minors. This issue infects all parental control obligations involving publishers.

data.title: A new record for California's highest tree
data.author: docmechanic
data.article_summary: 加州大学戴维斯分校的森林生态学家Hugh Safford在加州高塞拉地区徒步时意外发现了一种新的高海拔记录的杰弗里松树，其生长高度达到了12,657英尺，比此前记录高出1,860英尺。这一发现表明，随着气候变暖，杰弗里松正在向更高海拔迁移，得益于早融的雪和上升的气温，这些树木能够在以前无法生存的地方生长。研究还暗示，克拉克星鸦可能通过携带松树种子到高海拔地区促进了这一过程。尽管气候模型显示树木向高海拔迁移速度较慢，但鸟类的种子传播可能加速了这一进程。Safford计划进一步研究这种现象，强调实地观察对理解气候变化影响的重要性。

43736061.article_content:
Science News
from research organizations
A new record for California's highest tree
Highest Jeffrey pines ever recorded reflect a warming climate in the High Sierra
Date:
April 17, 2025
Source:
University of California - Davis
Summary:
A professor's casual hike in the High Sierra turned into a new elevation record for California's highest tree, the Jeffrey pine, which wasn't formerly known to grow at extreme elevations.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
UC Davis Professor Hugh Safford was hiking for pleasure in California's High Sierra when he stumbled upon a new elevation record for the Jeffrey pine, which may now be the state's highest-altitude tree. His serendipitous finding is published in
Madroño
,
a journal of the California Botanical Society.
Last September, at timberline along the south slopes of Mount Kaweah in Sequoia National Park, Safford paused to admire a foxtail pine, then a lodgepole pine -- trees he expected to see at such high elevations.
"Then I thought, 'What's that?'" said Safford, a forest ecologist in the UC Davis Department of Environmental Science and Policy. "I walk over, and it's a Jeffrey pine! It made no sense. What is a Jeffrey pine doing above 11,500 feet?"
The Jeffrey pine grows in upper montane areas throughout the Sierra Nevada and is the most common tree found around Lake Tahoe and Mammoth Lakes. It is not considered a traditional subalpine tree species, which inhabit the most extreme high elevations. Yet, Safford recorded Jeffrey pines as high as 12,657 feet elevation. That is 1,860 feet higher in elevation than the highest Jeffrey pine on record and even higher than lodgepole, limber and foxtail pines.
To date, none of the six traditional subalpine forest species have been collected above 12,034 feet. This suggests the Jeffrey pine is California's highest tree -- at least for the moment. Safford's work indicates that other species are growing higher than commonly used databases suggest.
The discovery signifies a changing climate amid California's highest peaks. As snow melts earlier and air temperatures rise, Jeffrey pine seeds are germinating on land they previously found frozen and inhospitable.
Moving on up
During his hike-turned-science-expedition, Safford found and examined 14 Jeffrey pines above 11,800 feet elevation, some of which were at least 20 years old. At least a dozen others were visible, but he was unable to visit them. He and researchers from his lab will return to the southern Sierra Nevada this summer to further research Jeffrey pines in the subalpine zone and what is driving their movement.
For now, Safford strongly suspects a bird -- the Clark's nutcracker -- is lending its well-known, high alpine gardening skills to the task of planting Jeffrey pine trees in the area. Much as this nutcracker does for whitebark pine trees, preliminary evidence suggests the bird carries fleshy Jeffrey pine seeds up the mountain from thousands of feet below, storing them in the High Sierra's "refrigerator" for an early summer snack.
Earlier snowmelt and warmer temperatures enable some of these Jeffrey pine seeds to not only germinate but to establish themselves as a new population on the mountain.
Leapfrogging trees
Species attempting to stay ahead of climate changes by moving uphill are doing so far too slowly to keep pace, climate modeling literature suggests. Yet the models do not account for the role of seed dispersals by birds and other species amid shifting windows of ecological opportunity.
"I'm looking at trees surviving in habitats where they couldn't before, but they're also dying in places they used to live before," Safford said. "They're not just holding hands and walking uphill. This crazy leapfrogging of species challenges what we think we know about these systems reacting as the climate warms."
Jeffrey pine trees are tolerant of both cold and drought, so while their lives along the slopes of Mount Kaweah are harsh and somewhat unexpected, their persistence is promising, Safford said.
Trees in real life
The discovery underscores a need for scientists to couple powerful technologies with direct observation. The trees Safford encountered were not detected by any available database, artificial intelligence platform, satellite or remote sensing technology.
"People aren't marching to the tops of the mountains to see where the trees really are," Safford said. "Instead, they are relying on satellite imagery, which can't see most small trees. What science does is help us understand how the world functions. In this case, where you see the impacts of climate change most dramatically are at high elevations and high latitudes. If we want our finger on the pulse of how the climate is warming and what the impacts are, that's where it will be happening first. We just need to get people out there."
This summer, Safford and his students will be out there, hiking along Mount Whitney, Mount Kaweah and Sequoia-Kings Canyon National Parks, identifying

The Labyrinth of Villa Pisani in Stra, suggestions of D'Annunzio and an intricate pathway
by
Redazione
, published on 24/06/2024
Categories:
Travel
/
Disclaimer
The Labyrinth of Villa Pisani in Stra is one of the largest labyrinths in Europe and is best known for two reasons: its presence in one of Gabriele D'Annunzio's most beautiful novels and the difficulty of its path, one of the most complex in the world.
It is known as the “queen of the Venetian villas.” and indeed,
Villa Pisani
in
Stra
is a significant, elegant, majestic presence; it is impossible not to notice it as one travels along Veneto Regional Road 11, or the long road that leads from the center of Venice, from Piazzale Roma, to the gates of Padua, skirting the
Brenta Canal
, along which stand several of the villas that in ancient times the Venetian patriciate had erected in these pleasant countryside as vacation spots away from the city chaos of Venice. The largest is Villa Pisani, whose origins date back to the
18th century
, when the
Pisani di Santo Stefano
, one of the richest families of the Venetian nobility Venetian, reached their apogee, even managing to express a doge,
Alvise Pisani
, who was first Venetian ambassador to Louis XIV’s France, after which he ascended to the doge’s throne in 1735, when Villa Pisani was under construction.
Construction of the complex began in 1721, when the Pisani family entrusted the task to architect
Gerolamo Frigimelica
(Padua, 1653 - Modena, 1732), also the author of the sumptuous Palazzo Pisani in the sestiere of San Marco in Venice, and then to his colleague
Francesco Maria Preti
(Castelfranco Veneto, 1701 - 1774), who succeeded Frigimelica after his death in 1732. It took a few years to see the work completed, which ended in 1756. The villa, however, remained with the Pisani for a short time: in the late 18th century, the time of the decline of the Serenissima, the family also suffered heavy setbacks, and the villa had to be sold off to meet the debts the Pisani had accumulated. Villa Pisani thus became the property of
Napoleon Bonaparte
, who in turn gave it to his stepson Eugene de Beauharnais. After the Restoration, it became the imperial villa of the Habsburgs, who spent long holiday stays here. Then, following the Unification of Italy, the villa became part of the property of the Savoy crown, and in 1884, after a period of neglect, it was turned into a museum.
Villa Pisani in Stra, aerial view. Photo: Ministry of Culture
The facade of the Villa Pisani. Photo: National Museum of Villa Pisani
The faux facade of the stables of Villa Pisani. Photo: National Museum of Villa Pisani
The Ballroom. Photo: Ministry of Culture
Giambattista Tiepolo,
Apotheosis of the Pisani Family
(1761-1762; fresco, 12.7 x 7.7 m; Stra, Villa Pisani)
Villa Pisani is an imposing structure that behind its sober
neoclassical façade
conceals dozens of rooms (there are 168 in all, although those that can be visited number around 30), including the spectacular
ballroom
where
Giambattista Tiepolo
frescoed the
Apotheosis of the Pisani Family
, one of the greatest masterpieces of the eighteenth century in the world. Attached to the villa is then a splendid 14-hectare
park
with stables, the 18th-century Coffee House, English grove, tropical greenhouses and one of the most famous
labyrinths inItaly
, the
Labyrinth of Villa Pisani
precisely, which also became famous because it is the protagonist of one of the best-known scenes in the novel
Il Fuoco
by
Gabriele D’Annunzio
, who visited the villa after its transformation into a museum, dedicating unforgettable pages to it. In the novel, the young protagonist, the poet Stelio Effrena, travels through the labyrinth together with his lover, the Foscarina, in a subtle game of love among the maze’s meandering paths: “A gate of rusty iron closed it, between two pillars bearing two Lovers riding dolphins of stone. There was no glimpse beyond the gate except the beginning of a medium and a kind of tangled and hard forest, a mysterious and thick appearance. From the center of the tangle rose a tower, and at the top of the tower the statue of a warrior seemed to stand at the lookouts. ’Have you ever entered a labyrinth?” asked Stelio to his friend. ’Never,’ she replied. They lingered to admire that fallacious game composed by an ingenious gardener for the delight of ladies and cicisbei in the time of calcagnini and guardinfanti. But neglect and age had inselvated it, saddened it; had stripped it of all semblance of gracefulness and equality; had changed it into a closed patch between brown and yellowish, full of inextricable ambiguities, wher

data.title: Synology Lost the Plot with Hard Drive Locking Move
data.author: motiejus
data.article_summary: Synology正在计划在2025年将其NAS设备锁定为仅能使用自家品牌的硬盘，这一举措引发了不满。过去，Synology的硬件质量较高，但现在却因限制使用第三方硬盘而受到批评。这种做法迫使用户购买Synology或等效硬盘，同时某些功能如去重、寿命分析和固件自动更新将被禁用。此外，创建存储池也会受到限制。相比其他品牌如QNAP和TrueNAS，Synology的Plus系列硬盘最大容量仅为16TB，而其他品牌已达到26TB。而且，在价格和交付速度上，Synology的硬盘也不占优势，这不仅增加了用户成本，还可能影响数据安全和硬盘替换的灵活性。长期来看，这种锁定策略还可能因Synology的生存问题影响硬盘供应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Synology NAS产品的优缺点及其竞争策略

不同观点：
• Renaud：认为Synology的NAS硬件和操作系统在初始设置后表现稳定，真正的优势在于其应用生态系统，如备份和多平台集成。然而，对家用或小型办公用户强制要求使用Synology认证的硬盘是不明智的，这会损害用户的好感和品牌忠诚度。

• PeterStuer：对Synology的性能满意，但对其通过产品分割和垂直锁定来最大化利润的策略不满，计划逐步淘汰Synology产品。

• dostick：批评Synology在磁盘空间管理和报警系统上的缺陷，尤其是无法将低空间阈值设置低于5%，以及低空间通知问题。多次反馈未得到解决，反映了公司对小而关键问题的忽视。

• kotaKat：怀念简单的Drobo产品，尽管遭遇了“突然死亡综合症”而转向QNAP，但对新产品的要求是简单易用，无需过多关注技术细节。

• bob1029：支持使用云存储策略，认为对于大容量媒体存储，云服务的质量和弹性无可比拟，且避免了维护本地硬件的麻烦。

• emmelaich：理解Synology对硬盘选择的谨慎态度，特别是考虑到西部数据“绿盘”系列的问题，但建议通过缩小价格差异和减少交货时间来改善销售策略。

• romanhn：对Ugreen NAS的新硬件产品感兴趣，认为其规格和定价有吸引力，可能是一个比Synology更好的选择。

• kyrofa：讨论了硬盘故障时的数据安全和恢复速度问题，认为用户应该提前准备备用硬盘，而非依赖紧急采购。

• nichos：希望硬盘制造商合作推出运行TrueNAS的NAS，而不是各自开发专有操作系统，认为TrueNAS更为成熟和可靠。

• dmoy：因Synology不支持某些企业级硬盘型号而退货，选择自行组装NAS并运行TrueNAS，获得更好的硬件规格和灵活性。

• codecraze：计划更换NAS，寻找支持自定义操作系统、6-8个硬盘位且小尺寸的产品，不希望再次使用大型桌面电脑作为NAS。

• mgsouth：基于过去在NAS厂商的工作经验，理解对硬盘测试和认证的重视，认为从技术角度看，不希望客户自行带入硬盘。

• ziml77：担心Synology将强制硬盘要求的策略应用到旧产品上，表示若发生此情况，将不会再次选择Synology产品。

• aborsy：询问是否可以通过DSM的btrfs发送快照到Linux服务器，关注数据的可移植性和开放性。

• j45：支持Renaud的观点，认为强制要求使用特定硬盘是不明智的，建议考虑其他制造商的产品。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Synology对硬盘选择的限制及其对用户体验的影响。
- 用户对Synology的应用生态系统表示赞赏，但对其硬件和软件策略的改变表示不满。
- 云存储与本地NAS的优劣对比，以及TrueNAS等替代方案的讨论。
- 对NAS产品的小型化、灵活性和可靠性的需求。
